conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Submission of Jordan Lake Watershed Boundary Revisions to NC DWQ Without Public Hearing or Comprehensive Survey
conflicts.summary: Following closed session near 10:00 PM, the Board split 3-2 on directing the Planning Director to submit a 2005 developer survey and 2006 planning memorandum revising Jordan Lake watershed overlay boundaries to state regulators.
conflicts.side_a_position: Immediately submit the 2005 Puckett & Associates survey, boundary maps, and January 6, 2006 Frank Duke memorandum to NC DWQ/EMC to cure a procedural defect on an existing map change.
side_a_arguments: The boundary change had already been placed on the zoning atlas/books in 2006 without completing required DWQ approval procedures, creating a short-term problem that needed immediate correction.
Addressing this specific boundary filing immediately does not preclude pursuing a broader comprehensive survey of Jordan Lake later and protects citizens' rights where action was taken in good faith.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose late-night action without a public hearing and instead pursue a uniform, comprehensive survey of the Jordan Lake shoreline.
side_b_arguments: Taking significant zoning/watershed action near 10:00 PM with no citizens in the room and without a public hearing is procedurally inappropriate.
Former Planning Director Frank Duke overstepped his authority by altering the watershed boundary without bringing the matter to the Board of County Commissioners.
Staff should obtain a uniform, comprehensive shoreline survey across that section of Jordan Lake because piecemeal boundary adjustments affect other property owners and jurisdictions.
conflicts.resolution: Motion carried 3-2 (Ayes: Cheek, Cousin Jr., Page; Nays: Heron, Reckhow).

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Removal and Re-Advertisement of Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority Appointments Under Term-Limit Policy (Item 10)
conflicts.summary: The Board split 3-2 on Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek's motion, seconded by Vice Chair Becky M. Heron, to remove and re-advertise the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority appointments because incumbent Steve Toler appeared to have served beyond the Board's three-consecutive-term limit policy, while Commissioners Michael D. Page and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. dissented.
conflicts.side_a_position: Remove the RDU Airport Authority appointment item and re-advertise the positions so the Board can follow its adopted term-limit policy and review all applicants before deciding whether to grant a waiver or revise the rule.
side_a_arguments: The Board previously adopted a policy resolution stating no citizen may serve more than three consecutive terms unless waived by the County Commissioners.
Appointment records differed on whether incumbent Steve Toler was appointed in 1999 or 2001, and Toler indicated he believed he was in his fourth two-year term.
Re-advertising lets the Board see what additional applicants come forward and examine whether the term-limit rule should be enforced or amended.
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed removing and re-advertising the RDU Airport Authority appointments instead of proceeding with the scheduled appointments.
side_b_arguments: Voted against the motion to remove and re-advertise (specific floor remarks by the dissenting commissioners were omitted in gaps of the transcript digest, though Board discussion noted that both incumbent appointees had served with distinction and maintained strong communication, and that a prior waiver had been granted when Toler was in line to chair the Authority).
conflicts.resolution: Motion to remove and re-advertise the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority appointments passed 3-2; Chair Reckhow clarified that already-applied incumbents would remain on the ballot when it returned.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: R-20 Rezoning / Development Application with Technical Ordinance Violation and Neighborhood Mediation Impasse
conflicts.summary: Commissioners deadlocked 2-2 over whether to vote to approve a disputed R-20 development application adjacent to game lands after a nine-month delay, amid planning staff findings of a technical ordinance violation and County Attorney warnings of litigation risk.
conflicts.side_a_position: Bring the R-20 application to a vote for approval on the floor.
side_a_arguments: Moved and seconded to place the approval motion before the Board following a 10-minute recess rather than leaving the matter unresolved indefinitely.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose approving the application as submitted.
side_b_arguments: The applicant returned after nine months without resolving neighborhood concerns or changing the plan.
Planning staff was not directly involved in neighborhood negotiations and identified a technical violation of the zoning ordinance.
The R-20 land adjacent to game lands should be redesigned with a more environmentally sensitive plan rather than approved in non-compliant form.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to approve failed on a 2-2 tie with Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek excused.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Durham County Animal Control Ordinance Anti-Tethering Restrictions and Pen Size Mandate
conflicts.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 on adopting Chapter 4 Animal Control Ordinance amendments restricting tethering and expanding unobstructed dog enclosure requirements.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt the amended anti-tethering and minimum pen-size ordinance while pairing implementation with an education campaign and APS/coalition fence assistance.
side_a_arguments: Animal Control Director Cindy Bailey testified from 19 years of field experience that the majority of cruelty prosecutions involved chained dogs with embedded collars, lack of shelter, or sanitation hazards.
Expanding minimum enclosure sizes (100 sq ft for <=20 lbs, 200 sq ft for >20 lbs) addresses neighbor odor and sanitation complaints where chained dogs soil a 10-foot radius.
Coalition and APS fundraisers, an education lead-in period, and periodic progress reports to the Board will help families transition and comply.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the new ordinance as lacking Durham-specific empirical proof and creating undue hardship for elderly and low-income residents.
side_b_arguments: Proponents relied on national anecdotal claims without Durham County computer statistics proving a widespread problem requiring a new ban.
Existing cruelty provisions already allow prosecution of embedded collars, abuse, and neglect, and the revised attended-leash rule could suffice.
The ordinance omits technical assistance or financial relief for elderly or low-income residents who cannot afford fencing and may no longer be able to legally keep a pet.
conflicts.resolution: Ordinance passed 4-1 with Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek dissenting; staff agreed to collect disaggregated impact data and provide periodic education-campaign reports.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Opposition to Proposed National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF) in Granville County / Butner
conflicts.summary: The Board split 4-1 on whether to strengthen its Environmental Affairs Board draft EIS comments into formal opposition asking the consortium to withdraw the proposed Butner NBAF site.
conflicts.side_a_position: Formally oppose locating the NBAF facility in Butner/Granville County and request that the consortium withdraw the proposal.
side_a_arguments: The Draft EIS rated the Durham/Butner area as moderate public health risk while Plum Island was the only candidate site rated low risk, and the facility should remain and be upgraded where it already exists.

Unanswered questions remained from the Butner public hearing regarding safety, security, potential airborne/airplane spills, and evacuating or protecting frail and confined residents at nearby Butner institutions.
Granville County residents clearly voiced opposition to hosting the facility.
conflicts.side_b_position: Submit the Environmental Affairs Board's technical Draft EIS comments by the August 25 deadline without taking a formal vote of opposition at this stage.
side_b_arguments: While respecting Granville County residents, the process was only at the Draft EIS comment stage and taking an outright opposition stance before the final EIS was premature compared to submitting technical comments.
conflicts.resolution: Motion carried 4-1 with Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek dissenting; the Chair and County Manager were directed to circulate the strengthened opposition letter to the Board before signing.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Deferral of Residential Development / Zoning Proposal (Parking, Carrying Costs, and Planning Commission Recommendation)
conflicts.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 over deferring a residential development proposal for two weeks after debating sewer line carrying costs, parking reduction/two-car garage design, and adherence to the Planning and Zoning Commission's recommendation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Defer the development proposal for two weeks for additional revisions and direction on parking and project design.
side_a_arguments: Sufficient direction was provided to the applicant regarding parking and garage design to bring the item back in two weeks.
Deferral allows time to address infrastructure and carrying-cost issues without immediately dismissing the Planning and Zoning Commission's recommendation.
side_b_arguments: Dissented from the deferral vote following debate over parking reduction, project design, and Planning and Zoning Commission input.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to defer for two weeks carried 4-1 with Becky M. Heron dissenting.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Durham County Memorial Stadium Architectural Design Contract ($646,275)
conflicts.summary: Commissioners split 3-1 over executing a $646,275 architectural design contract with DTW Architects and Planners for renovations to Durham County Memorial Stadium following Shaw University's withdrawal from participation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the design contract to upgrade Durham County Memorial Stadium and attract broader community and event use.
side_a_arguments: Renovations will turn the stadium into a facility Durham County can be proud of.
Proposals for stadium usage are already being received and improvements will generate increased multi-event use.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose spending $646,275 on stadium renovation design.
side_b_arguments: Stadium improvements are not the best use of the property or county funds.
Shaw University's withdrawal from its participation agreement leaves the county bearing more of the cost.
conflicts.resolution: Contract approved 3-1 with Lewis A. Cheek voting Nay (Chair Ellen W. Reckhow absent/excused).

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: $4.5 Million General Fund Balance Advance for Durham County Memorial Stadium Renovations (Item 7H)
conflicts.summary: During consideration of the July 23, 2007 consent agenda, Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek objected to advancing $4.5 million from General Fund balance for the Durham County Memorial Stadium renovation project and asked to be recorded as voting No, prompting the Board to pull Item 7H and approve it 3-1.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advance $4.5 million from General Fund balance (to be reimbursed via spring 2008 financing) to move forward with Durham County Memorial Stadium renovations.
side_a_arguments: Funding advances the planned Memorial Stadium renovation capital project ahead of spring 2008 financing reimbursement.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose advancing $4.5 million in county funds for the Memorial Stadium renovation project.
side_b_arguments: Reiterated prior opposition, arguing the stadium renovation is not a good expenditure of county funds.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 3-1 on a separate voice vote (Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. excused).

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Cost and Fiscal Timing of DSS Lease Agreement with Genesis Home
conflicts.summary: Commissioners split 3-1 over approving a $45,000-per-year (plus utilities) DSS lease for 4,400 square feet at Genesis Home, weighing family support needs against taxpayer sensitivity before the November bond referendum.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the DSS lease with Genesis Home to support family reunification and frontline social workers.
side_a_arguments: Provides a warm, comfortable family environment to help dysfunctional or disadvantaged families re-enter mainstream society.
Supports social workers handling gang violence, poverty, and school-related family challenges who are frequently asked to work across Durham without extra compensation.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the lease as an expensive expenditure given taxpayer frustration and upcoming bond votes.
side_b_arguments: Paying $45,000 per year plus utilities and phone/computer lines for 4,400 square feet represents a high-dollar facility commitment.
Taxpayers are already strained and approaching a November bond referendum, risking perceptions of excessive county spending.
conflicts.resolution: Motion carried 3-1 with Vice Chair Becky M. Heron dissenting.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.summary: Commissioners split 3-1 on enacting a ban on roadway solicitation in unincorporated Durham County paired with a resource list for deputies, debating pedestrian safety and outreach versus potential punitive enforcement against homeless individuals without a parallel city ordinance.
conflicts.side_a_position: Enact the county roadway solicitation ban paired with a social-service resource sheet for deputies.
side_a_arguments: Soliciting on county arterials with 45-55 mph traffic is physically unsafe for individuals in or beside the roadway.
The ordinance is not intended to jail people, but to serve as a compassionate vehicle for deputies to distribute a condensed resource list connecting people to mental health and shelter services.
County action could encourage the City of Durham to adopt a similar ordinance.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose enacting the county ban at this time without a joint city-county framework and stronger homeless services.
side_b_arguments: Most roadway solicitation occurs inside city limits, yet the City of Durham has not enacted a corresponding ordinance.
Homeless residents on the streets are in dire need of help and services, and passing a ban signals law enforcement to enforce it in a way that feels unwelcoming to the community.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 3-1 on first reading with Michael D. Page voting Nay; because fewer than four affirmative votes were cast, the ordinance was scheduled for a second reading on April 23.

conflicts.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
conflicts.issue: Immediate Authorization vs. Deferral of $100,000 Comprehensive Jordan Lake Shoreline Survey
conflicts.summary: Commissioners disagreed sharply over whether to immediately authorize $100,000 for a detailed county-wide Jordan Lake shoreline survey (with 10-to-50-foot intervals) or defer the expenditure to the newly elected Board taking office in December.
conflicts.side_a_position: Defer action on the $100,000 comprehensive survey until the new Board convenes and considers it in the budget or future meetings.
side_a_arguments: Three board members had already submitted two registered surveys and additional maps requested by the Division of Water Quality (DWQ) to address the immediate boundary issue.

The comprehensive survey would not be completed in time to affect DWQ's review of the pending submission, and there was no identified funding source or urgency to commit $100,000 at the outgoing Board's final meeting.
conflicts.side_b_position: Immediately approve the County Manager's recommendation and budget amendment for an independent, comprehensive shoreline survey.
side_b_arguments: As noted by County Manager Mike Ruffin, the earlier surveys relied on points more than 1,000 feet apart (with the first lacking normal-pool documentation) and were unlikely to satisfy DWQ.

Commissioner Becky M. Heron read resident correspondence from the 450-home Chance's Ridge HOA urging an independent survey to protect drinking water and avoid opening the door to piecemeal developer surveys.
Delaying action would leave a six-month-plus unresolved issue in the incoming Board's lap and risk costlier regional water quality problems.
conflicts.resolution: A motion to defer was seconded, followed by a seconded substitute motion to approve the County Manager's recommendation; however, the transcript ends at 03:55:08 during Manager Ruffin's explanation before a vote was taken.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 24, 2008 Regular Session presided over by Chair Ellen W. Reckhow—the final regular meeting for outgoing Commissioners Lewis A. Cheek and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.—the Board unanimously approved prior meeting minutes, recognized Kids Voting Durham and award-winning Tax Administration staff, and honored the outgoing commissioners before reading an extensive consent agenda prior to a truncated middle section. Following a closed session on employee performance and watershed boundary matters, the Board engaged in a sharp policy debate over whether to immediately approve a $100,000 comprehensive Jordan Lake shoreline survey recommended by County Manager Mike Ruffin. One commissioner moved to defer the $100,000 survey to the incoming Board, arguing two registered surveys already submitted to the state Division of Water Quality (DWQ) adequately addressed the pending boundary issue, while Commissioner Becky M. Heron (citing Chance's Ridge HOA concerns) and another commissioner backing a substitute motion argued the prior surveys lacked sufficient reference points and immediate comprehensive action was necessary to protect drinking water. The available transcript ends while Manager Ruffin was explaining his recommendation for the third survey, prior to any recorded final vote on the substitute motion or motion to defer.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow noted the deletion of Item 8D and Friday packet additions. After correcting a name spelling in the October 27 minutes ('Walt') and confirming with County Manager Mike Ruffin that a letter to Commerce Secretary Jim Fain regarding the housing program was awaiting site closeout, the Board unanimously approved the October 27 Regular Session and November 3 Work Session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Kids Voting Durham Election Day 2008 Efforts (Item 5A)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow recognized Kids Voting Durham Coordinator Carolyn Kruger and participating teachers and site volunteers for engaging children in voting and poll-site administration during the November 2008 election.

agenda_items.title: Tax Administration Staff and Department Awards (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Kim Simpson recognized staff members Darnell Allen (top score on the N.C. Property Mappers Association exam) and Kevin Locklear (2008 President's Pride Award). The Board also celebrated the Tax Administration Department's second consecutive Joseph E. Hunt Distinguished Jurisdiction Award for Outstanding Achievement in Tax Administration and Public Service.

agenda_items.title: Farewell Recognition of Outgoing Commissioners Lewis A. Cheek and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow and colleagues honored outgoing Commissioners Lewis A. Cheek and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. for four years of service, highlighting expanded substance abuse treatment and an adult system of care that had placed 16 formerly homeless individuals into housing. Both outgoing commissioners offered farewell remarks thanking staff, colleagues, and family.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through I and Remaining Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow began reading the long consent agenda—covering a City-County tax interlocal amendment, October property tax releases/refunds, a NetApp storage network purchase from ePlus Inc., Public Health grants ($11,036 breast/cervical cancer control and $3,000 March of Dimes), $361,335 in DSS crisis intervention funds, Duke University Health System Board nominations (Mike Ruffin, Dr. Iris Smith, Rev. Kenneth Hammond), and the Parkwood Branch Library lease renewal (pulled by Chair Reckhow)—before the transcript truncated through the middle of the session.

agenda_items.title: Debate on Comprehensive Jordan Lake Shoreline Survey and Budget Amendment ($100,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a closed session on employee performance and watershed boundary matters, commissioners debated a motion to defer a proposed $100,000 comprehensive Jordan Lake shoreline survey (with 10-to-50-foot intervals) until the incoming Board took office versus a substitute motion to immediately approve County Manager Mike Ruffin's recommendation for the survey. Commissioner Becky M. Heron read a Chance's Ridge HOA email urging immediate approval, while County Manager Ruffin warned the two prior developer-funded surveys—using points over 1,000 feet apart—lacked enough reference points to pass DWQ review; the transcript ends before a vote was called.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 10, 2008 Special and Regular Sessions presided over by Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the Durham Board of County Commissioners reviewed the Greenfire Development Phase 2 downtown redevelopment and parking partnership, directed the County Attorney to draft a downtown parking resolution following a public hearing, adjusted the County Manager's salary to $179,000 unanimously, and split 3-2 on submitting Jordan Lake watershed boundary revisions to state regulators. After an afternoon briefing on tying County parking deck assistance (scheduled to begin construction in November 2013) to four Greenfire projects and a public hearing where Downtown Durham Inc. projected a need for at least 4,000 new downtown spaces over the next decade, the Board voted unanimously to have the County Attorney draft a parking resolution. Following a closed session regarding personnel and Time Warner Cable litigation, the Board voted 3-2—with Commissioners Lewis A. Cheek, Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr., and Michael D. Page voting Aye, and Chair Ellen W. Reckhow and Vice Chair Becky M. Heron dissenting (Nays)—to direct the Planning Director to submit the January 6, 2006 Frank Duke memorandum and 2005 Puckett & Associates survey revising Jordan Lake watershed overlay boundaries to the N.C. Division of Water Quality and Environmental Management Commission without first holding a public hearing. The Board concluded by unanimously adjusting County Manager Mike Ruffin's salary to $179,000 effective November 17, 2008.

agenda_items.title: Special Session: Greenfire Development Phase 2 Downtown Redevelopment Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Greenfire Development representatives presented updates on downtown mixed-use projects including Rogers Alley, while county staff and Laura Jensen outlined a draft partnership framework for a downtown parking deck adjacent to the County's Court Annex and Judicial buildings starting construction in November 2013. Under the draft terms, County parking support would be conditioned on Greenfire completing four downtown developments (Chapel Hill Street parking redevelopment, Woolworth office building, 109 S. Corcoran St., and eight smaller commercial properties totaling 77,000 sq ft), cost caps, County design approval, and M/WBE compliance.

agenda_items.title: Regular Session Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes, and Assistant Manager Introduction (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow noted a revised closed session item and announced Veterans Day events, the November 12 Long Range Transportation Plan hearing, the November 18 South Regional Library groundbreaking, and the Durham Youth Summit. The Board unanimously approved the October 13, 2008 Work Session minutes, and County Manager Mike Ruffin introduced the Assistant County Manager prior to a truncated middle segment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Downtown Parking and Greenfire Partnership Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) President Bill Kalkhof and Government Relations Director Melissa Norton presented an inventory showing roughly 870 peak-hour spaces currently available downtown and projecting at least 4,000 new spaces needed over the next decade. disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Submission of Jordan Lake Watershed Boundary Revisions to NC DWQ Without Public Hearing or Comprehensive Survey
disagreements.summary: Following closed session near 10:00 PM, the Board split 3-2 on directing the Planning Director to submit a 2005 developer survey and 2006 planning memorandum revising Jordan Lake watershed overlay boundaries to state regulators.
disagreements.side_a_position: Immediately submit the 2005 Puckett & Associates survey, boundary maps, and January 6, 2006 Frank Duke memorandum to NC DWQ/EMC to cure a procedural defect on an existing map change.
side_a_arguments: The boundary change had already been placed on the zoning atlas/books in 2006 without completing required DWQ approval procedures, creating a short-term problem that needed immediate correction.
Addressing this specific boundary filing immediately does not preclude pursuing a broader comprehensive survey of Jordan Lake later and protects citizens' rights where action was taken in good faith.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose late-night action without a public hearing and instead pursue a uniform, comprehensive survey of the Jordan Lake shoreline.
side_b_arguments: Taking significant zoning/watershed action near 10:00 PM with no citizens in the room and without a public hearing is procedurally inappropriate.
Former Planning Director Frank Duke overstepped his authority by altering the watershed boundary without bringing the matter to the Board of County Commissioners.
Staff should obtain a uniform, comprehensive shoreline survey across that section of Jordan Lake because piecemeal boundary adjustments affect other property owners and jurisdictions.
disagreements.resolution: Motion carried 3-2 (Ayes: Cheek, Cousin Jr., Page; Nays: Heron, Reckhow).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its late-October 2008 Regular Session presided over by Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the Durham Board of County Commissioners passed all observed motions unanimously, with no split or contested votes. The Board honored late acclaimed photojournalist and longtime North Carolina Central University public relations director Alex Rivera, proclaimed Adoption Month, and unanimously adopted a high-performance green building resolution requiring LEED Gold for new county buildings over 10,000 square feet, LEED Silver for 4,000 to 10,000 square feet, and LEED Certified for major renovations. Following a truncated middle segment covering the consent agenda, commissioners unanimously approved a zoning map amendment aligning a 3.5-acre Durham County sliver of a 21-acre Wake/Durham site with industrial/office R&D land use, closed out the 2002 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Scattered-Site Housing Program while requesting follow-up on future housing grant applications, endorsed the 2011–2017 Transportation Improvement Program (TIP) local priority list with requested review of an Erwin Road pedestrian segment, and read board and commission appointment selections.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Tribute to Alex Rivera, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the meeting (greeting attendees as Monday, October 27, 2008) and led a tribute mourning acclaimed photojournalist and NCCU public relations pioneer Alex Rivera, noting his civil rights work and exhibition at the N.C. Museum of History. The Board unanimously approved the October 6, 2008 Work Session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Adoption Month Proclamation and Veterans Day Ceremony Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read the Adoption Month proclamation alongside Department of Social Services staff, noting the need for adoptive homes for foster youth (with Victoria Peterson signed up to speak). Remarks also highlighted the upcoming November 11 Veterans Day ceremony on the courthouse steps.

agenda_items.title: High-Performance Green Building Design Resolution (LEED Standards)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sustainability Manager Tobin Fried presented a resolution developed with the Environmental Affairs Board formalizing county green-building standards in alignment with the County's Greenhouse Gas Action Plan (50% emissions cut from 2005 levels by 2030). The Board unanimously mandated at least LEED Gold for new public buildings over 10,000 sq ft, LEED Silver for 4,000–10,000 sq ft, LEED Certified for major renovations, USGBC checklist use, and brownfield/transit-conscious siting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A through 6H, Partial Transcript)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow began reading Consent Agenda items—including September property tax releases/refunds, OPEB funds, several NC DHHS Public Health grants (with Item 6E Plain Talk and Item 6G family planning/contraceptives pulled for separate consideration), and a $2,242+ reserved fund balance appropriation—before the transcript truncated through the middle of the session.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Amendment for Bisected Durham/Wake Site (WSP Sells)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Beth Lewis of WSP Sells requested a zoning map amendment for approximately 3.5 acres in Durham County forming part of a 21-acre parcel bisected by the Wake County line, noting the larger Wake portion in Cary's ETJ would be annexed by Cary while the Durham sliver would align with its industrial land-use designation for office/R&D development. With no opposition from adjacent owners, the Board closed the public hearing and unanimously approved the rezoning.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Closeout of 2002 CDBG Scattered-Site Housing Program (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Leah Consulting Group President Brian Crawford presented the closeout of the 2002 Community Development Block Grant Scattered-Site Housing Program (covering 13 homes and uncompensated extra work after funds were exhausted). Commissioners discussed severe ongoing home repair needs among low-income residents, asked staff to circulate a letter signaling intent to apply for future funding, and unanimously approved the closeout after closing the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: 2011–2017 Transportation Improvement Program (TIP) Local Priority List (Item 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Planner Ellen Beckman and Bicycle/Pedestrian Planner Dale McKeel presented Attachment B listing Durham County's proposed highway, bicycle/pedestrian, transit, and fixed-guideway priorities for the 2011–2017 TIP ahead of DCHC MPO regional review. Commissioners discussed corridor connectivity and requested staff review adding or reordering a missing Erwin Road segment near a school before unanimously approving the priority list.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed Farmland Protection Advisory Board participation (including Robert B. Glenn Jr.) and read appointment selections for the Animal Control Review Board, Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau/TDA, Farmland Protection Advisory Board, Historic Preservation Commission, Library Board of Trustees, Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee, Transportation Advisory Board, and Workforce Development Board before adjourning at 9:27 PM.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes of the October 6, 2008 Work Session.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved rezoning ~3.5 acres in Durham County to match its industrial land-use plan designation for office/R&D development alongside the Cary ETJ portion.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries in hand' / unanimously); mover and seconder were not spoken on the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the closeout of the 2002 Community Development Block Grant Scattered-Site Housing Program following a public hearing with no speakers present.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 13, 2008 Regular Session presided over by Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved all formal actions unanimously by voice votes, with no split or contested votes. The Board proclaimed the 50th anniversary of the Durham chapter of The Links, Incorporated and 'Pull the Plug' Week for adolescent pregnancy prevention, adopted a 25th-anniversary resolution honoring Urban Ministries of Durham, and began recognizing a Social Services state award before a truncated middle portion of the transcript. In the second half of the session, commissioners unanimously approved a rezoning for an office/institutional development near Bethpage after securing additional committed elements for a pond trail, outdoor employee eating area, and double silt fencing, and unanimously ratified the 2007 Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR). The Board postponed consideration of the 2011–2017 Transportation Improvement Program (TIP) local priority list for two weeks due to staff absence and amid discussion of highway trust fund shortfalls and Fayetteville Road/East End Connector priorities, and adjourned following an economic-development closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of September 22, 2008 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow welcomed attendees to the October 13, 2008 Regular Session and noted no agenda adjustments or announcements. The Board unanimously approved the September 22, 2008 Regular Session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: 50th Anniversary of Durham Chapter of The Links, Incorporated
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read a proclamation declaring the week of October 13, 2008 as Durham Chapter of Links Week, honoring the 16 women who chartered the chapter in 1958 (including former Commissioner Josephine Clement) and its recent $100,000 Ford Foundation grant. Chapter President June Michelle, Vice President Faith Tate Williams, and 50th Anniversary Chair E. Joyce Grant accepted the proclamation.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: 'Pull the Plug' Week (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read a proclamation designating October 19–25, 2008 as 'Pull the Plug' Week in support of the Durham Coalition on Adolescent Pregnancy Prevention (DCAPP) and Let's Talk Month. Presenters encouraged families to reduce youth media use by one to three hours per day and participate in workshops at NCCU and the Hayti Heritage Center.

agenda_items.title: Resolution: 25th Anniversary Week of Urban Ministries of Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Michael D. Page read a resolution celebrating Urban Ministries of Durham's 25th anniversary, noting its annual provision of over 180,000 meals, 40,000 shelter nights, pantry food, and clothing supported by 2,700 volunteers and 83 cents per dollar in direct services. An Urban Ministries representative thanked the County for its public-private partnership.

agenda_items.title: Social Services NCACC Award Recognition (Item 8, Partial Transcript)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow introduced Item 8 recognizing Durham County and the Department of Social Services for honors received at the August North Carolina Association of County Commissioners (NCACC) annual meeting, before the middle of the transcript truncated.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Amendment for Office Development Near Bethpage
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Applicant representative Craigie Sanders discussed stormwater detention (two- and ten-year storm events), impervious surface, Traffic Impact Analyses, and architectural compatibility with the adjacent Bethpage development and nearby corporate sites (IBM, Cree, AT&T, Goodwill, BFI). After the applicant agreed to add committed elements for a stormwater-pond trail, an outdoor employee seating area, and double silt fencing, the Board unanimously approved the rezoning.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: 2007 Comprehensive Plan Amendment Evaluation and Assessment Report (Item 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff member Joseph Parley summarized the 2007 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR), reviewing underway and scheduled policies, one City-adopted plan amendment requiring ratification (a Lowe's Grove project), six proposed new departmental policies, and updated 2007 NCDOT traffic counts. After opening and closing the public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously approved the report.

agenda_items.title: 2011–2017 Transportation Improvement Program (TIP) Local Priority List (Item 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Noting Transportation Planner Ellen Beckman's absence, Chair Reckhow and commissioners discussed bicycle/pedestrian priorities, unfunded segments of Fayetteville Road and the East End Connector, and federal and state highway trust fund shortfalls. Chair Reckhow asked staff to examine an additional pedestrian item and postponed the item for two weeks.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deferred / Postponed two weeks without vote

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Economic Development (Item 14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to adjourn to closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business or industry location/expansion. Returning at 10:22 PM, Chair Reckhow reported direction was given to staff with no formal action taken, and adjourned.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 22, 2008 Regular Session presided over by Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the Durham Board of County Commissioners passed every motion unanimously by voice vote, with no split or contested votes. The Board recognized the 20th anniversary of Cooperative Extension's Welcome Baby program and proclaimed Minority Enterprise Development Week (October 6–10, 2008) before approving Consent Agenda Items 7A through 7O—including over $4.81 million in IT computer and telecommunications replacement funding, a $398,000 Farmland Preservation Trust Fund grant for Tilley Farm, $194,548 for BOCC chamber technology upgrades, $367,004 for the Human Services Complex, and a $248,265 East Main Street 500-block demolition contract. Commissioners reviewed the draft Work First Plan ahead of an October 13 public hearing and unanimously adopted an Animal Control Ordinance amendment transferring animal fee billing and collection to the Tax Administration Office effective November 1, 2008. After pulling Item 7P because a Durham Center nominee to the Criminal Justice Partnership Act Advisory Board lived outside Durham County, the Board unanimously approved the three compliant appointments (Sheriff's designee, District Court Judge, and Superior Court Judge slots) pending inquiry into an in-county Durham Center nominee, then concluded with a closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow clarified that Consent Item 7O referenced the September 16, 2008 conservation easement draft rather than the September 12 draft, announced a September 25 public meeting on Main Library renovations, welcomed Boy Scout Troop 486, and thanked HR Director Marqueta Welton for the employee service-awards luncheon. The Board unanimously approved three sets of minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: 20th Anniversary of Welcome Baby Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read a proclamation honoring the 20th anniversary of Cooperative Extension's Welcome Baby Family Resource Center, highlighting its support for families with children aged birth to five and announcing the October 12 'A Great Day in Durham' celebration at Durham Central Park.

agenda_items.title: Resolution: Minority Enterprise Development Week (October 6–10, 2008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read a resolution recognizing October 6–10, 2008 as Minority Enterprise Development Week and reaffirming Durham County's M/WBE ordinance (Section 8-132) and good-faith contracting policies. Pamela Gills accepted the resolution and previewed the week's events including Shop a Minority Business Day.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 7A through 7O)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved Consent Items 7A through 7O (pulling Item 7P for review), covering tax administration contracts (Cox & Co. $90,500; RS&M Appraisal $150,000), $93,760.20 in SAP licenses, $4,338,640 for IT computer replacement and $475,000 for IT telecommunications, a $398,000 Tilley Farm farmland preservation grant, capital amendments for BOCC chamber technology ($194,548) and the Human Services Complex ($367,004), a $248,265 East Main Street demolition contract with Environmental Holdings Group LLP, library design amendments for Southwest ($7,100) and South Regional ($27,800), and the September 16 UDO Section 8.7.2.B.2 conservation easement.

agenda_items.title: Draft Work First Plan Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters reviewed the draft Work First Plan and requested an October 13, 2008 public hearing. Commissioners raised questions about job retention benchmarks (noting a 49% overall average), monitoring continuity, adding page numbers, and updating 2006-07 graduation statistics before the October hearing.

agenda_items.title: Ordinance Amending Durham County Animal Control Ordinance (Tax Office Fee Collection)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Kim Simpson presented an ordinance effective November 1, 2008 converting animal fees into a tax and moving billing and collection from Animal Control to the Tax Office. The change pairs notices with monthly motor vehicle bills, adds online and kiosk payment options, and shares non-vaccinated pet records with Animal Control; the Board approved the ordinance unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Criminal Justice Partnership Act Advisory Board Appointments (Item 7P) and Board Selections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Confirming that the County's residency policy did not exempt the Durham Center slot on the Criminal Justice Partnership Act Advisory Board and that nominee Robert Robinson lived outside Durham County, the Board unanimously approved the three compliant appointments (Sheriff's designee, District Court Judge, and Superior Court Judge slots) and asked the Durham Center for an in-county nominee before considering any policy waiver. Ballot selections for another board were also read.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Legal and Economic Development Matters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4) for attorney-client consultation and business/industry location discussions. Upon returning at 9:50 PM, Chair Reckhow reported direction was given to staff with no action taken, and adjourned.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the ordinance effective November 1, 2008 converting animal fees into a tax administered and collected by the Tax Office.

votes.item_title: Criminal Justice Partnership Act Advisory Board Appointments (Three Compliant Slots, Excluding Durham Center Slot) (Item 7P)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the Sheriff's designee, District Court Judge, and Superior Court Judge appointments to CJPAAB while holding the Durham Center slot to seek a Durham County resident.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.executive_summary: At the September 9, 2008 Joint City-County Committee meeting presided over by Chair Ellen W. Reckhow (with Deputy County Manager Carolyn Titus filling in for County Manager Mike Ruffin), members unanimously approved the August 12 minutes and received four informational briefings with no split or contested votes. Cultural Master Plan Advisory Board representative Josh Parker reviewed implementation progress—including growth in the Bimbé Festival to roughly 7,000 attendees, nonprofit management scholarships at Duke, a capital-project evaluation tool, and the Durham History Museum feasibility study—while warning of funding uncertainty after June 2009 depending on the November prepared food tax referendum. City and county staff summarized FY 2008 and FY 2009 Results-Based Accountability (RBA) mini-grants ($113,000 budgeted jointly per year) and proposed partnering with Triangle United Way to hire and supervise a new RBA coordinator and unify nonprofit grant tracking. Coordinator Tim Henderson detailed the federal Project Safe Neighborhoods three-tier anti-gang initiative ($1.25 million across enforcement, prevention/intervention, and reentry), and Chair Reckhow reported on newly enacted state legislation allowing fee-based express NCDOT development traffic reviews before members discussed voter confusion around the 'prepared food tax' ballot phrasing.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Addition, and Approval of August 12 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow welcomed members, noted Deputy County Manager Carolyn Titus was filling in for County Manager Mike Ruffin, and added a discussion on expediting transportation reviews after Item 4. The committee unanimously approved the August 12 meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Cultural Master Plan Advisory Board Annual Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Josh Parker reported on the 15-year Cultural Master Plan's 2008–09 goals, citing the revitalized Bimbé Festival at Durham Athletic Park (~7,000 attendees, 25% more local artists), 38 Duke nonprofit management tuition scholarships, a Vermont-modeled cultural capital decision tool, and Preservation Durham portable exhibits ahead of the Durham History Museum feasibility study. He noted only one year of interlocal funding remained after June 2009 and emphasized coordinating messaging around the fall prepared food tax referendum.

agenda_items.title: Results-Based Accountability (RBA) Mini-Grants Report and United Way Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Strategic Initiatives Director Julie Brenman and County Budget Technician Laura Jensen reported that the City and County jointly fund $113,000 annually for RBA mini-grants, awarding 15 grants (~$95,000, one unexecuted) in FY 2008 and 14 grants ($102,425) in FY 2009. Following staff departures, they outlined a proposed City-County-United Way agreement under which Triangle United Way would hire and supervise the RBA coordinator and explore shared nonprofit data systems.

agenda_items.title: Project Safe Neighborhoods Anti-Gang Initiative and Gang Assessment Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Grant Coordinator Tim Henderson reviewed the U.S. Department of Justice Project Safe Neighborhoods three-tier anti-gang initiative totaling $500,000 for law enforcement ($380,000 services), $500,000 for prevention/intervention ($370,000 services), and $250,000 for reentry ($193,000 services). Officials discussed school attendance gains at seven target schools with layered social workers and nurses, agency turf/coordination challenges, and Crime Cabinet representation.

agenda_items.title: Expediting NCDOT Transportation Reviews and Prepared Food Tax Messaging
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow reported on speaking with NCDOT Division Engineer Wally Bowman about sluggish traffic-impact reviews for development proposals and noted the General Assembly had recently authorized an optional developer-paid fee for express NCDOT review. Members also discussed informational mailers for the November referendum, warning that the statutory label 'prepared food tax' confused voters who mistakenly feared groceries would be taxed rather than prepared meals.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes of the August 12, 2008 meeting.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 8, 2008 Regular Session presided over by Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the Durham Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the consent agenda and the FY 2008–09 Secondary Road Construction Program, and passed a contested Animal Control Ordinance anti-tethering amendment on a 4-1 split vote. On the Consent Agenda (5A–5E, 5G), the Board approved the amended Cultural Master Plan interlocal agreement (paying $125,000 upon invoice), an RDU FAA grant, $19,700 in RBA grants, a $145,000 Urban Ministries shelter contract, and Cherry, Bekaert & Holland LLP as external auditors ($105,000), followed by unanimous approval of the annual Secondary Road Construction Program presented by NCDOT. After pulling the Animal Control Ordinance amendments from consent due to post-hearing revisions specifying minimum unobstructed dog pen sizes (100 sq ft for dogs 20 lbs or under; 200 sq ft for dogs over 20 lbs) alongside anti-tethering limits, the Board voted 4-1 to adopt the ordinance—with Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, Vice Chair Becky M. Heron, Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr., and Commissioner Michael D. Page voting Aye, and Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek voting Nay after arguing the ordinance lacked local statistical evidence and failed to protect elderly or low-income pet owners who could not afford fencing. The session closed after board appointments and a closed session on E.T. Development Corp. litigation (08 CVS 3340) and business location.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, Campaign Report (Item 3A), and Library Awards (Item 4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the meeting, noted Item 5F was deleted, Item 5H was moved to regular agenda Item 6A, and Item 5A was amended to pay $125,000 upon invoice presentation. Civic leaders from 'A Taste for Durham's Future' previewed the fall 1% prepared food tax campaign logo, and County Engineer Glenn Whisler and Library Director Skip Auld accepted recognition for two state and national design awards won by North Regional Branch Library.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 5A through 5E, 5G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved the Cultural Master Plan interlocal agreement and advisory board, an RDU Airport Authority FAA grant offer, $19,700 in RBA grants for the Durham Center, Public Health, and DSS, a $145,000 Urban Ministries homeless shelter contract, external auditor selection of Cherry, Bekaert & Holland LLP ($105,000), and upset-bid surplus property offers at 2600 Lincoln Street and 540 Belt Street.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2008–09 Secondary Road Construction Program (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: NCDOT District Engineer Tasha Johnson presented the FY 2008–09 Secondary Road Construction Program, noting seven roads remained on the unavailable right-of-way list. After opening and closing the public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously approved the program.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Amendments to Animal Control Ordinance (Anti-Tethering and Dog Pen Space)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled from consent due to post-hearing revisions clarifying that Chapter 4 Section 5(f) space minimums apply to dogs (100 sq ft unobstructed for dogs 20 lbs or under; 200 sq ft for dogs over 20 lbs), Assistant County Attorney Marie Inserra and Animal Control Director Cindy Bailey reviewed the anti-tethering proposal, enforcement experience, and enclosure standards. Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek argued the county lacked local statistical evidence and failed to provide financial aid for elderly or low-income owners, while the remaining four commissioners emphasized cruelty/sanitation concerns and APS fence-assistance efforts; the ordinance passed 4-1.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board read appointment selections including Marshall Dennis and Harriet Sander to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council, an appointee to the Library Board of Trustees, and Kathy Hines, Virginia Martin, and Barbara Messer to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee. Commissioners then adjourned to closed session on County of Durham v. E.T. Development Corporation (08 CVS 3340) and business location before returning at 9:33 PM to adjourn with no action taken.

votes.item_title: FY 2008–09 Secondary Road Construction Program (Item 6)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the FY 2008–09 NCDOT Secondary Road Construction Program for Durham County following a public hearing with no speakers.

votes.item_title: Amendments to Durham County Animal Control Ordinance (Anti-Tethering and Minimum Dog Pen Space)
votes.notes: Passed 4-1 by voice vote ('Motion carries 4-1 with Commissioner Cheek dissenting'). Mover and seconder spoke at 01:28:38 and 01:28:48 without being named aloud by the Chair.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted amendments to Chapter 4 of the Durham County Code restricting unattended animal tethering and establishing minimum unobstructed enclosure sizes of 100 sq ft (dogs <=20 lbs) and 200 sq ft (dogs >20 lbs), alongside periodic progress reports on education and APS fence assistance.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Durham County Animal Control Ordinance Anti-Tethering Restrictions and Pen Size Mandate
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 4-1 on adopting Chapter 4 Animal Control Ordinance amendments restricting tethering and expanding unobstructed dog enclosure requirements.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the amended anti-tethering and minimum pen-size ordinance while pairing implementation with an education campaign and APS/coalition fence assistance.
side_a_arguments: Animal Control Director Cindy Bailey testified from 19 years of field experience that the majority of cruelty prosecutions involved chained dogs with embedded collars, lack of shelter, or sanitation hazards.
Expanding minimum enclosure sizes (100 sq ft for <=20 lbs, 200 sq ft for >20 lbs) addresses neighbor odor and sanitation complaints where chained dogs soil a 10-foot radius.
Coalition and APS fundraisers, an education lead-in period, and periodic progress reports to the Board will help families transition and comply.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the new ordinance as lacking Durham-specific empirical proof and creating undue hardship for elderly and low-income residents.
side_b_arguments: Proponents relied on national anecdotal claims without Durham County computer statistics proving a widespread problem requiring a new ban.
Existing cruelty provisions already allow prosecution of embedded collars, abuse, and neglect, and the revised attended-leash rule could suffice.
The ordinance omits technical assistance or financial relief for elderly or low-income residents who cannot afford fencing and may no longer be able to legally keep a pet.
disagreements.resolution: Ordinance passed 4-1 with Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek dissenting; staff agreed to collect disaggregated impact data and provide periodic education-campaign reports.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 25, 2008 Regular Session presided over by Vice Chair Michael D. Page (with Chair Ellen W. Reckhow excused at the Democratic National Convention and Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek excused by a 3-0 vote), the three present commissioners—Page, Becky M. Heron, and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.—passed all motions unanimously with no split or contested votes. The Board approved prior August minutes, presented a retirement resolution honoring Chief Deputy C. Wes Crabtree's 28-year Sheriff's Office career, and proclaimed September as Alcohol and Drug Addiction Recovery Month. On the Consent Agenda (Items 7A–7I and 7L), commissioners unanimously approved $79.17 million in 2007 General Obligation Bond appropriations and $500,000 in 2003 bond transfers for Durham Public Schools capital projects, an ambulance purchase ($99,574), Cooperative Extension grants, and an initial slate of prepared food tax projects contingent on the November 4 referendum. Following a well-attended public hearing on proposed Animal Control anti-tethering amendments (whose middle portion was truncated in the transcript), the Board agreed by consensus to review the Animal Control Advisory Committee's finalized 'attended' definition at the September 2 work session, and concluded by unanimously approving the FY 2008–09 Rural Operating Assistance Program (ROAP) transit grant application.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Absent Commissioners, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Vice Chair Michael D. Page noted Chair Ellen W. Reckhow had been excused at the prior meeting and obtained a unanimous voice vote from the three present commissioners to excuse Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek. Following an announcement of the August 26 Women's Equality Day ceremony, the Board unanimously approved the August 4 Work Session and August 11 Regular Session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Retirement Resolution for Chief Deputy C. Wes Crabtree (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Sheriff and Vice Chair Page recognized Chief Deputy Carlton Wesley Crabtree upon his September 1, 2008 retirement after 28 years of service beginning as a jailer in 1980, noting he was the first Durham County Sheriff's Office member to graduate from the FBI National Academy (1999). Crabtree thanked the Board and community.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Alcohol and Drug Addiction Recovery Month (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Page read a proclamation designating September 2008 as Alcohol and Drug Addiction Recovery Month under the theme 'Join the Voices for Recovery: Real People, Real Recovery,' and presented it to Ellen Holman.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 7A through 7I and 7L)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved Consent Items 7A–7I and 7L, including July property tax releases/refunds, Smart Start Cooperative Extension grants ($34,468 and $11,970), two Public Health grants ($15,004 and $15,000), a $79,170,128 appropriation of 2007 GO bonds plus $550,000 county contribution and $3.95M DPS land acquisition shift, a $500,000 2003 GO bond transfer from W.G. Pearson Elementary to Morehead ($400,000) and Lakeview ($100,000) elementary schools, a $99,574 EMS ambulance contract, Work First Plan status, and the initial prepared food tax project slate.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Proposed Animal Control Ordinance Anti-Tethering Amendments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens spoke for and against the proposed anti-tethering ordinance across a public hearing whose middle portion was truncated in the transcript, debating animal cruelty enforcement versus responsible tethering rights. After closing the hearing, commissioners noted the Animal Control Advisory Committee had already revised the definition of 'attended' to address Commissioner Cheek's earlier concerns and agreed to continue review at the September 2 work session so absent members could review the hearing tape.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2008–09 Rural Operating Assistance Program (ROAP) Grant Application (Item 10)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the consolidated FY 2008–09 ROAP grant application for elderly/disabled, rural general public, and Work First transitional transportation services across local human-service partner agencies. After questioning cost-per-mile/cost-per-client discrepancies (which staff reported had been corrected) and closing a public hearing with no speakers, the Board unanimously approved submitting the application to NCDOT.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 11, 2008 Regular Session presided over by Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the Durham Board of County Commissioners welcomed back County Manager Mike Ruffin, unanimously approved the consent agenda, and split 4-1 to formally oppose locating the federal National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF) in nearby Butner (Granville County). After recognizing high school participants in the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition's Student Construction Training Program and proclaiming August 26 as Women's Equality Day, the Board unanimously passed Consent Items 7A–7F—renewing the 10-Year Plan to End Homelessness memorandum of agreement and receiving the annual Open Space and Trails and risk-management reports. Following public comment on Item 8 (partially truncated in the middle of the transcript), the Board voted 4-1 to strengthen the Environmental Affairs Board's Draft EIS comment letter to formally oppose the Butner NBAF site and request withdrawal of the proposal—with Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, Vice Chair Becky M. Heron, Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr., and Commissioner Michael D. Page voting Aye, and Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek voting Nay after arguing the Board should submit technical EIS comments rather than taking an outright opposition stance. Commissioners then discussed 2009 legislative goals—including phasing in a higher compulsory school attendance age (17 then 18) and direct school-district sales tax refunds—before adjourning after an economic-development closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Welcome to County Manager, Excusal Motion, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow welcomed County Manager Mike Ruffin back and thanked Deputy County Manager Carolyn Titus for serving as acting manager. The Board voted unanimously to excuse Chair Reckhow from the August 25 meeting (to attend the Democratic National Convention), announced the August 25 animal-tethering public hearing, and unanimously approved the July 28, 2008 Regular Session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of 2008 Student Construction Training Program (Item 5)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Michael D. Page led recognition of high school students participating in the 2008 Student Construction Training Program in partnership with the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition, highlighting their summer on-the-job construction training and community housing contributions.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Women's Equality Day 2008 (Item 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read a proclamation designating August 26, 2008 as Women's Equality Day in commemoration of the 19th Amendment and presented it to Kimberly Moore/Monroe of the Durham County Women's Commission, which planned to honor 20 notable Durham County women on August 26.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 7A through 7F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved Consent Items 7A–7F, including the 2007 Durham Open Space and Trails Commission annual report, retirement/disposal of law enforcement surplus property, one-year renewal of the MOA with the City and Triangle United Way for the 10-Year Plan to End Homelessness, two Cooperative Extension budget amendments ($2,225 pollution control and $18,000 youth substance abuse prevention), and the FY 2007–08 liability claims and subrogation recovery report (Risk Manager Kathy Wesson).

agenda_items.title: Findings and Position on Proposed National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF) in Granville County (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed Environmental Affairs Board, Health Department, and Emergency Management findings on the Draft Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) for the proposed NBAF site in Butner (Granville County), followed by public comment (truncated in the middle). Chair Reckhow moved—with majority backing from Heron, Cousin Jr., and Page—to strengthen the Environmental Affairs Board's draft letter to oppose the Butner site and request withdrawal of the proposal due to moderate public health risk and proximity to frail institutionalized populations, while Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek voted no, preferring to limit action to technical EIS comments; the motion passed 4-1.

agenda_items.title: 2009 Durham County Legislative Agenda Planning (Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Craig Ray outlined the 2009 NCACC and local legislative timeline. Commissioners discussed submitting a phased proposal to raise the compulsory school attendance age (to 17 after two years and 18 after four years), direct sales tax refunds to school districts for construction, and school construction impact fees, while a community speaker urged securing state court-fee funding for youth rehabilitation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Economic Development
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding the location or expansion of business or industry. Returning at 9:55 PM, the Board reported direction was given to staff with no action taken, and adjourned.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Opposition to Proposed National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF) in Granville County / Butner
disagreements.summary: The Board split 4-1 on whether to strengthen its Environmental Affairs Board draft EIS comments into formal opposition asking the consortium to withdraw the proposed Butner NBAF site.
disagreements.side_a_position: Formally oppose locating the NBAF facility in Butner/Granville County and request that the consortium withdraw the proposal.
side_a_arguments: The Draft EIS rated the Durham/Butner area as moderate public health risk while Plum Island was the only candidate site rated low risk, and the facility should remain and be upgraded where it already exists.

Unanswered questions remained from the Butner public hearing regarding safety, security, potential airborne/airplane spills, and evacuating or protecting frail and confined residents at nearby Butner institutions.
Granville County residents clearly voiced opposition to hosting the facility.
disagreements.side_b_position: Submit the Environmental Affairs Board's technical Draft EIS comments by the August 25 deadline without taking a formal vote of opposition at this stage.
side_b_arguments: While respecting Granville County residents, the process was only at the Draft EIS comment stage and taking an outright opposition stance before the final EIS was premature compared to submitting technical comments.
disagreements.resolution: Motion carried 4-1 with Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek dissenting; the Chair and County Manager were directed to circulate the strengthened opposition letter to the Board before signing.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the July 28, 2008 Regular Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners highlighted the opening of the new Durham Access Center on the Durham Regional Campus and recognized Tax Administrator Kimberly Simpson and her staff alongside Durham City Council members for achieving a 98.87% county tax collection rate, second-highest among North Carolina's ten largest counties. The Board unanimously (5-0) excused a commissioner from the upcoming August 4 work session, approved four sets of minutes with a minor correction, and endorsed educational outreach surrounding a proposed cultural arts referendum (noting no public funds would be used for advocacy). Commissioners also voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the Bangu Property major site plan and preliminary plat for a 51-lot single-family subdivision on Guess Road and approved the 2007 property tax settlement and 2008 tax charge. Following a brief discussion deferring one board appointment until a full board was present, the Board adjourned into a closed session to consult with legal counsel and discuss business location matters, taking no action afterward.

agenda_items.title: Excusal from August 4 Work Session and Opening Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner requested to be excused from the August 4 work session, which the Board approved unanimously. Chair Ellen W. Reckhow noted the morning opening of the Durham Access Center for mental health and substance abuse services on the Durham Regional Campus and announced upcoming public meetings on the National Bio-Agro Defense Facility, Durham Neighborhood College applications, and Main Library renovations.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: On June 9, 2008, Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened by noting Deputy County Manager Carolyn Titus was serving as Acting County Manager while Mike Ruffin recovered from emergency surgery, and the Board passed a resolution honoring botanist Elizabeth 'Liz' Pullman for her service on the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission. All formal votes on the evening's agenda passed unanimously (5-0), including the May 27 minutes, the consent agenda (notably a $207,766-$225,000 SmithGroup Main Library renovation study), and pulled items 6C and 6D funding a joint domestic violence Assistant District Attorney and $92,800 for telephone system upgrades. The Board held a lengthy public hearing on the FY 2008-2009 Recommended Budget featuring appeals for Cultural Master Plan, Durham History Museum, and ENCORE after-school funding, and adopted UDO text amendments on townhouse/shopping center driveway naming (TC0717) and stormwater/stream buffer standards (TC0721) by 5-0 votes while referring a height-requirement text change (TC0801) back to planning staff. The Board also appointed Commissioner Michael D. Page as NACo voting delegate (5-0) and entered closed session (5-0) on business expansion matters without subsequent action.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Minutes Approval, and Resolution Honoring Elizabeth Pullman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow announced County Manager Mike Ruffin's recovery from emergency surgery, noted Carolyn Titus as Acting County Manager, and added a NACo voting delegate appointment to the agenda before the Board unanimously approved the May 27 minutes. The Board then presented a resolution honoring botanist Elizabeth 'Liz' Pullman for her years on DOST and her work preserving over 2,000 acres of open space.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A, 6B, 6F, 6G) and Pulled Items (6C, 6D)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved consent items 6A (Home and Community Care Block Grant plan), 6B (Joyce Arches to Animal Control Advisory Committee), 6F (SmithGroup PLLC Main Library architectural study up to $225,000), and 6G (Design District Review Team annual report) in one unanimous vote. Items 6C (joint city-county Assistant DA for domestic violence) and 6D ($92,800 transfer to the telephone system upgrade project, bringing its total to $1,502,800) had been pulled by Elivonia Allison, who was absent when called, and were approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2008-2009 Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens addressed the Board for two minutes each regarding the FY 2008-2009 recommended budget, with speakers including Jane Goodridge advocating for Cultural Master Plan and Durham History Museum funding and Leisha Johnson supporting the ENCORE middle school after-school program. Staff also outlined nonprofit funding review criteria tied to Results-Based Accountability and the Board's retreat priorities of reconnecting youth, economic empowerment, and sustainability, with deliberations scheduled to continue Thursday.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change - Driveway Names (TC0717)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner T.E. Austin presented text amendment TC0717 revising Articles 12 and 13 of the UDO to permit naming driveways in townhouse developments and shopping centers for public safety purposes. With no members of the public signed up to speak, the Board closed the hearing and approved the amendment unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change - Stormwater (TC0721)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner T.E. Austin and the County Attorney presented TC0721 revising UDO stream buffer and watershed protection standards to align with the city's NPDES permit, apply buffer rules to all qualifying intermittent and perennial streams without a 25-acre drainage minimum, and retain 'operation and maintenance agreement' language alongside 'agreement and covenants.' Alan Lang had addressed stormwater earlier during the budget hearing and departed, and the Board unanimously adopted the amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change - IL Compact District Height Requirements (TC0801)

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 27, 2008 Regular Session, the Board celebrated a 48% reduction in Durham County child abuse rates and 100% accuracy in Food and Nutrition Services, proclaimed June as Hunger Awareness Month, and received County Manager Mike Ruffin's FY 2008-2009 Recommended Budget ($792.5 million total across 21 funds, $683.5 million General Fund). Following a continued public hearing on an Andrew Avenue residential rezoning, commissioners secured added developer commitments—including a 5,500-square-foot minimum lot size, skimmer stormwater basins, sidewalks, and a second tot lot serving affordable housing units—before approving the rezoning unanimously (5-0). The Board also voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the minutes and a second lease extension amendment for Scarborough & Hargett Funeral Home incorporating a late-payment remedy and confirming schedules for county building and parking deck work. The meeting concluded with ballot appointments to five boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments, Announcements, Minutes, and Hunger Awareness Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow criticized late distribution of revised committed elements for items 8 and 9, directing planning staff to include critical materials in advance agenda packets. Commissioners applauded a 48% drop in county child abuse rates and 100% Food and Nutrition Services accuracy, unanimously approved three sets of minutes, and proclaimed June as Hunger Awareness Month (noting 37,170 residents, or 15.6%, living at or below poverty).

agenda_items.title: FY 2008-2009 Recommended Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Mike Ruffin presented a $792.5 million total recommended budget across 21 funds, including a $683.5 million General Fund (a 3.45% increase). Highlighting client success stories from Welcome Baby and CJRC's Project Restore, Ruffin noted $200.5 million in projected property taxes and $50.5 million in sales taxes (reflecting a $2.96M Medicaid swap drop offset by a $5.4M county Medicaid share reduction), with 64 cents of every dollar dedicated to education and human services and over 13 cents to public safety.

agenda_items.title: Continued Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change (Andrew Avenue / Joint Jurisdiction)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reopened a continued public hearing from the prior month with the developer's representative addressing committed elements: a 5,500-square-foot minimum lot size, sidewalks on Andrew Avenue and one side of internal streets, and skimmer basins for stormwater management. Vice Chair Becky M. Heron and Chair Reckhow pressed the applicant on livability for affordable housing residents, securing a formal committed element for a second 40x40 fenced tot lot with a play structure on the eastern side of the stream/sheet D2 before unanimously approving the rezoning (subject to City Council concurrence).

agenda_items.title: Second Lease Amendment: Scarborough & Hargett Funeral Home, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney explained that the second lease amendment extended the existing lease and added a new section 3 remedy for late payments, confirming it would not delay the county building and parking deck timeline. Staff reported the parking deck design was proceeding alongside the building design once space counts are resolved and that demolition of the U-Haul building was planned for summer before the Board approved the amendment.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Vice Chair Heron endorsed Jim Hedrick's reappointment to the Memorial Stadium Authority, the clerk announced the Board's ballot appointments to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, Durham City-County Appearance Commission, Durham Planning Commission, Memorial Stadium Authority, and Women's Commission, and the meeting adjourned at 8:41 PM.
