meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Joint Meeting with Durham Delegation
meetings.executive_summary: On April 30, 2008, the Durham Board of County Commissioners held a joint legislative meeting with members of the Durham General Assembly delegation to review the county's priorities for the 2008 short session. Key topics included school construction funding and developer voluntary contributions, a proposed 1% prepared food tax referendum, prioritized state court funding for probation audits, evidence preparation, witness protection, and JCPC continuation funding. Commissioners strongly opposed state cost-shifting to counties—specifically Senate Bill 1513 on state road responsibilities, court filing fee mandates on county social services and animal control actions, and a budget provision requiring the final third of counties including Durham to purchase state-selected courthouse phone systems. The Board also requested technical fixes to the property tax circuit-breaker law and urged pilot testing before any statewide consolidation of mental health Local Management Entities (LMEs); no formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: School Capital Funding, Sales Tax, and Proposed 1% Prepared Food Tax
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed school construction funding pressures, sales tax revenues, and bills affecting voluntary developer contributions ($2.5 million offered over two years). They also reviewed breakdown projections for a proposed 1% prepared food tax referendum following an April 17 joint meeting with the City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Court System Funding Priorities, JCPC, and Filing Fee Mandates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners outlined prioritized court funding requests—covering a probation management audit, evidence preparation, witness protection, additional court staff, and JCPC continuation funding—alongside concerns about DNA lab backlogs delaying cases. They also asked legislators for a technical correction repealing a last-minute budget provision requiring counties to pay court filing fees for essential animal control and social services actions.

agenda_items.title: Senate Bill 1513 (DOT Road Maintenance) and Courthouse Phone System Mandate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representing county concerns echoed by the NC Association of County Commissioners, commissioners opposed Senate Bill 1513, arguing NCDOT should operate more efficiently rather than shifting road responsibilities and costs onto counties. They also objected to a July 1 mandate forcing the final third of counties—including Durham, unlike Wake and Mecklenburg—to pay for AOC-selected courthouse telephone systems, requesting a technical repeal.

agenda_items.title: Tax Circuit Breaker Corrections and Mental Health LME Consolidation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners conveyed the Tax Administrator's support for technical corrections to the 2007 property tax circuit breaker legislation and discussed regional conservation facility partnerships. Regarding proposals to consolidate mental health Local Management Entities (LMEs), the Board urged testing changes via pilot programs rather than statewide mandates and highlighted funding equity for high-contributing counties.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 28, 2008 Regular Session, the Board approved all five recorded votes unanimously (5-0), including the April 7 and April 14 minutes and the consent agenda—which adopted the FY 2008-2009 HUD Annual Action Plan (restoring Criminal Justice Resource Center funding), renewed ambulance franchises, and urged NC State University to preserve public recreation at Hill Forest. The Board held a public hearing on Case 05-45 (Angier/Andrew Haven, 120 single-family lots on 33.5 acres in RSM zoning), questioning the lack of a minimum lot size and omitted Open Space and Trails Commission recommendations. Commissioners also directed staff to brief the Board on civil penalty enforcement limits in the sedimentation ordinance following a court ruling, approved (5-0) deal points to purchase the Lakewood YMCA property for $250,000 with a 15-year leaseback, and adopted (5-0) the 2008 Short Session Legislative Agenda (featuring a 1% prepared food tax referendum—though one commissioner voiced reservations about taxing everyday residents versus hotel guests—and school impact fees) before entering closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments, Early Voting Announcements, Minutes, and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board deleted item 11, added item 13A, noted record-breaking early voting ahead of the May 6 primary, and unanimously approved the April 7 and April 14 minutes. Commissioners then issued proclamations for Foster Care Month, Mental Health Month (presented with Doug Fuller of the Durham Center), and Older Americans / Senior Results-Based Accountability.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 9A-9I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved the consent agenda, accepting the 2007 Development Review Board report, Smart Start ($49,088) and Environmental Health ($19,241) budget amendments, and the FY 2008-2009 HUD Annual Action Plan restoring CJRC funding pending City Council action. The package also approved three-year ambulance franchise renewals, March 2008 tax releases, a resolution supporting public access to NCSU's Hill Forest, a Civic Center lease relocation, and a SunTrust vehicle/equipment loan at 2.675%.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Case 05-45 (Andrew Avenue)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Scott Whiteman presented RD Construction Inc.'s request to rezone 33.5 acres along Andrew Avenue from RS-20 and CG to RSM for 120 single-family lots (recommended 8-3 by the Planning Commission). Commissioners questioned why RSM multifamily zoning was used (the applicant cited comprehensive plan density minimums), why there was no minimum lot size commitment, and why several Open Space and Trails Commission recommendations were omitted; final action occurred in a subsequent continued hearing.

agenda_items.title: Sedimentation and Erosion Control Enforcement Briefing Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a court ruling interpreting state law so that daily civil penalties cannot be rendered until a violation is cleaned up—creating a disincentive to remediate—commissioners requested a staff memo and work-session briefing on enforcement fixes. Staff noted the county shifted to seeking immediate injunctive relief and planned to pursue a statutory amendment during the 2009 long session.

agenda_items.title: Lakewood YMCA Property Purchase and Leaseback Deal Points (Item 13A)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented three-part deal points to purchase the Lakewood YMCA property for $250,000 and enter a 15-year leaseback with the YMCA, providing faster county facility capacity than buying land and building new. Commissioners praised the County Manager and 'Save the Y' neighborhood efforts before approving the deal points unanimously.

agenda_items.title: 2008 Short Session Legislative Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed the proposed 2008 short session legislative package ahead of Wednesday's legislative breakfast, including a 1% prepared food tax referendum (with added open space and trails projects), Crime Cabinet priorities, school construction impact fee authorization, and water supply protection. One commissioner voiced reservations about a prepared food tax affecting everyday residents rather than a hotel occupancy tax on visitors, after which the Board unanimously approved the legislative agenda as modified.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client, Economic Development, and Confidential Matters)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(4) to consult with legal counsel and discuss business location or expansion. Upon reconvening, the Board reported giving staff direction with no action taken and adjourned at 9:36 PM.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the 2008 legislative agenda with open space/trails additions to the proposed 1% prepared food tax breakdown; one unidentified speaker noted preference for considering a hotel occupancy tax over a prepared food tax.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: During the April 14, 2008 Regular Session, the Board celebrated National County Government Week by honoring volunteer board and commission members and receiving an NCACC Outstanding County Program Award for Durham DSS's Long-Term Care Web Center. Commissioners also read resolutions supporting continued state funding for the Criminal Justice Resource Center and Juvenile Crime Prevention Council and reviewed the draft HUD Annual Action Plan (questioning Urban Ministries Community Kitchen funding shifts and HOME consortium allocations). All four recorded votes passed unanimously (5-0): approving closed session and regular session minutes, rezoning 76.5 acres at Redwood Road and I-85 from Industrial Light to Residential Rural following abandonment of the Northern Durham Freeway corridor, entering closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) for a personnel review, and adjusting the Clerk to the Board's salary to $79,365 after finding her compensation 11% below comparable North Carolina county clerks.

agenda_items.title: Minutes Approval, Volunteer Recognitions, and NCACC Program Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After reminding residents of early voting registration opportunities, the Board unanimously approved closed session minutes and three sets of regular session minutes. Commissioners presented exemplary volunteer awards to citizens including Steve Tuller and youth volunteer Shabani, and received the NCACC Outstanding County Program Award for the DSS Long-Term Care Web Center.

agenda_items.title: Resolutions Supporting CJPP (CJRC) and JCPC State Continuation Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Michael D. Page and Becky M. Heron read resolutions urging the General Assembly to restore Criminal Justice Partnership Program and Juvenile Crime Prevention Council funding to the state continuation budget. CJRC Director Gudrun Parmer emphasized reduced recidivism since 1994 Structured Sentencing, while public speaker Victoria Peterson urged stronger county partnerships with existing community ex-offender programs.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2008-2009 HUD Annual Action Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In the portion of the hearing following a transcript gap, commissioners asked why funding for Urban Ministries' Community Kitchen was cut from one grant stream (staff explained they avoided dual-source funding and recommended full operating support under ESG) and requested figures on additional HOME consortium funding received due to county participation. With no public speakers signed up, the hearing closed ahead of scheduled April 28 action.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change - Northern Durham Freeway at I-85
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented a Joint City-County Planning Committee-initiated rezoning of 76.5 acres south of Redwood Road and west of I-85 from Industrial Light to Residential Rural in the Falls/Jordan watershed critical area, prompted by abandonment of the Northern Durham Freeway thoroughfare (Planning Commission recommended 7-4). Commissioners asked about the three-acre minimum lot size, absence of rural-tier tree cover rules, and upcoming traffic counts before closing the hearing and approving the rezoning unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Wake County Research and Production Service District Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board completed ballot selections for four appointments to the Durham-Wake County Research and Production Service District: Ron Hunter, Ray Gunner, Robert D. Tier Jr., and Tom Caldwell.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Clerk to the Board Performance Salary Adjustment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to evaluate a public officer's performance. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 24, 2008 Regular Session, the Board passed all eight recorded votes unanimously (5-0). Commissioners excused Michael D. Page from the April 7 work session, approved the February 25 minutes, issued proclamations for Child Abuse Prevention Month and National County Government Week, and approved consent items 7A, 7B, 7D (creating a joint city-county Sustainability Manager FTE with an $800,000 program budget), and 7G. Commissioners pulled and individually approved (5-0) three additional consent items: an $820,294 University Ford vehicle contract for the Sheriff's Office and Animal Control (after probing Crown Victoria mileage and urging future fuel-efficiency reviews), a capital project amendment creating 10 Durham Public Schools projects using advanced 2007 GO bond funds (including the Hillside cafeteria), and a federal funding commitment letter for Lincoln Community Health Center renovations after public comment from Victoria Peterson. The Board also adopted a UDO text amendment on sidewalk design flexibility (5-0) after clarifying NCDOT right-of-way authority on rural county roads, and adjourned to closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Excusal of Commissioner Page, Announcements, Minutes, and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Deputy County Manager Carolyn Titus filling in for the manager, the Board unanimously excused Commissioner Michael D. Page from the April 7 work session, announced a March 25 NC Turnpike Authority hearing on the Triangle Parkway, and approved the February 25 minutes. Commissioners then issued proclamations for April as Child Abuse Prevention Month (citing 2,129 DSS assessments and 391 substantiated cases in 2007) and April 6-12 as National County Government Week.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 7A, 7B, 7D, 7G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved the unpulled consent items: setting an April 28 public hearing on closing TW Alexander Drive (7A), February 2008 property tax releases and refunds (7B), an interlocal agreement with the City of Durham creating one Sustainability Manager FTE and an $800,000 FY 2007-2008 sustainability program budget split equally with the city (7D), and the second amendment to the interlocal agreement with Durham Public Schools (7G).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7C: Sheriff's Office and Animal Control Vehicle Contract ($820,294)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow pulled the $820,294 University Ford vehicle contract to question 15.5 mpg Crown Victoria fuel mileage and SUV/heavy-truck selections. Sheriff's Office and Animal Control staff explained patrol gear capacity, inclement weather needs, and horse-trailer towing requirements, and commissioners supported the purchase while directing future fleet fuel-efficiency evaluations.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7E: Capital Project Amendment for 10 DPS 2007 GO Bond Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed creating 10 new Durham Public Schools capital projects funded via advanced county 2007 GO bond funds (including the Hillside High School cafeteria). Vice Chair Heron asked about reusing the old school facility rather than demolishing it, and Commissioner Page asked whether the projects would eliminate classroom trailers in fast-growing areas before the Board approved the amendment unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 7F: Lincoln Community Health Center Federal Funding Commitment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled item 7F to voice concerns about long-time Durham seniors facing crowding at Lincoln Community Health Center. Commissioners emphasized that securing federal renovation funds and reimbursement would expand care for sick and disabled residents, approved the commitment letter unanimously, and asked staff to draft a thank-you letter to Congressman David Price.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change - Sidewalks (Section 12.4)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented a City Public Works-requested UDO text amendment granting design flexibility for sidewalks in Section 12.4 to ensure pedestrian safety and ADA compliance (recommended 11-0 by the Planning Commission). Vice Chair Heron asked how sidewalk rules apply to rural county roads with drainage ditches; Medlin explained NCDOT controls county rights-of-way and determines feasibility or additional right-of-way needs, after which the Board closed the hearing and approved the amendment unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client, Economic Development, and Confidential Information)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), (a)(4), and 143-1310E. Upon returning to open session, the Board reported giving staff direction with no action taken and adjourned at 9:26 PM.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: On March 10, 2008, the Board honored Chair Ellen W. Reckhow for receiving the Dorothy B. Graham Child Care Leadership Award and issued a Social Work Month proclamation before passing all six formal votes unanimously (5-0). The consent agenda (excluding pulled items 6B and 6H) authorized $12.1 million in GO Public Improvement Bonds and $34.09 million in GO School Bonds, approved a $1 million Clean Water Management Trust Fund grant for the Hollow Rock Duke Acquisition, funded a joint city-county domestic violence Assistant DA, and adopted the Downtown Master Plan. After Elivonia Allison pulled items 6B ($234,411.50 for C.C. Spaulding Elementary) and 6H (DPS Performance Learning Center lease at Northgate Mall) over rising lease costs, the Board approved both (5-0) and requested a joint meeting with the School Board to review 2003 and 2007 bond balances. Commissioners also unanimously approved (5-0) an age-restricted residential rezoning (after securing unamendable 90% age-restriction covenants and a traffic signal contribution) and the fourth technical UDO update (5-0), made advisory board appointments, and exited closed session to appoint Kimberly Simpson as Tax Administrator at a $97,500 salary (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Dorothy B. Graham Award Recognition, and Social Work Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board added a closed session to the agenda, and Commissioner Michael D. Page recognized Chair Ellen W. Reckhow on winning the Dorothy B. Graham Child Care Leadership Award for championing the ENCORE program, state childcare subsidies, and the childcare resource center. Commissioners also heard environmental stewardship remarks, issued a Social Work Month proclamation, and heard public comments regarding working families' income gaps for Medicaid and food stamps.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A, 6C-6G, 6I-6O)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After confirming the Downtown Master Plan imposed no financial obligations on the county, the Board unanimously approved the consent agenda excluding pulled items 6B and 6H. Major approved items included $12,100,000 in GO Public Improvement Bonds and $34,090,000 in GO School Bonds, the $1,564,000 Hollow Rock Duke Acquisition project (with $1M Clean Water grant), a $15,000 city-funded domestic violence Assistant DA agreement, Register of Deeds imaging conversion, surplus property sales, and an ambulance replacement contract amendment.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 6B (C.C. Spaulding Elementary) and 6H (DPS Performance Learning Center Lease)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speaker Elivonia Allison questioned rising annual lease costs ($73,602 to $81,780 per year) for the DPS Performance Learning Center at Northgate Mall (6H) alongside the $234,411.50 GO bond reserve appropriation for C.C. Spaulding Elementary (6B). Commissioners highlighted that 100% of Performance Learning Center graduates placed into Durham Tech or four-year colleges, unanimously approved both items, and directed staff to arrange a joint meeting with the School Board to review 2003 and 2007 bond fund balances.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: 90% Age-Restricted Residential Development
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed strengthened restrictive covenants locking in a 90% age restriction (unamendable to reduce the restriction and enforceable by the HOA, property owners, and adjacent properties including the school), reduced projected Creekside Elementary student generation and peak-hour traffic compared to 57 by-right single-family homes, and a developer contribution toward an intersection traffic signal. Vice Chair Becky M. Heron noted she did not obtain her preferred 100% age restriction or five-unit reduction, but joined the unanimous 5-0 approval due to the added commitments.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change - Fourth Comprehensive Technical Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented the fourth comprehensive technical update to the UDO—clarifying language, updating flood hazard provisions, fixing typos, and adding definitions—backed by a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. With no public speakers, the Board closed the hearing and adopted the technical amendments unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments, Closed Session, and Appointment of Kimberly Simpson as Tax Administrator
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board appointed four members to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee and James M. Miller to the Public Health Board, noted a tentative April 28 joint meeting with DPS, and entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6). Upon reconvening, the Board voted unanimously to appoint Kimberly Simpson to a two-year term as Tax Administrator through June 30, 2010 at a $97,500 salary with prior NC service credit for leave, and adjourned at 9:25 PM.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved $234,411.50 GO bond reserve appropriation for C.C. Spaulding Elementary and Northgate Mall operational lease for DPS Performance Learning Center following public comment by Elivonia Allison.

votes.item_title: Item 11: UDO Text Change - Fourth Comprehensive Technical Update
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted fourth comprehensive technical update to the Unified Development Ordinance.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) - Tax Administrator Appointment)
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to consider appointment of a new Tax Administrator.

votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Kimberly Simpson to a two-year term as Tax Administrator until June 30, 2010 at $97,500 salary with credit for prior NC jurisdiction service toward sick leave and vacation.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its February 25, 2008 regular session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners recognized GIS supervisor David Goldstein for his North Carolina Property Mappers Association achievement, highlighted Cooperative Extension grants ($1,595,571) and volunteer hours ($260,050), celebrated the NCACC Centennial resolution, and recognized awards for the Quintiles expansion and North Regional Branch Library. Following a truncated middle section covering a residential development proposal with two-car garages, sewer line carrying costs, and Planning and Zoning Commission recommendations, the Board voted 4-1 to defer the matter for two weeks, with Ellen W. Reckhow, Lewis A. Cheek, Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr., and Michael D. Page voting Aye and Becky M. Heron voting Nay in dissent. The Board then unanimously (5-0) approved comprehensive plan amendments for Hebron Road Elementary School (A0717) and Page Road Corporate Center (A0716), and following a public hearing unanimously (5-0) adopted three two-thirds general obligation bond orders totaling $12,100,000 ($500,000 library facility bonds, $4,950,000 public building bonds, and $6,650,000 school bonds).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Excusal from Monday Work Session

agenda_items.title: Announcements: Adult Care Home Committee & Cooperative Extension Grants
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners solicited applicants for the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, which inspects local adult care homes in pairs. The Board also recognized Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers for presenting two honorary checks representing at least 12 grants totaling $1,595,571 (June 30, 2006 through December 2007) and $260,050 in volunteer hours across Welcome Baby, Agricultural Extension, and the Soil and Water Conservation District.

agenda_items.title: Approval of February 11, 2008 Regular Session Minutes

Commissioners also invited attendees to view the new sliding wall at the Center for Senior Life before approving the minutes as corrected.

agenda_items.title: Recognition: David Goldstein (North Carolina Property Mappers Association)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Tax Administrator Kim Simpson introduced GIS Supervisor David Goldstein, who completed the state-mandated certified mapper examination and earned an academic achievement award from the North Carolina Property Mappers Association. The Board presented Goldstein with a recognition plaque.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Celebrating 100 Years of County Unity (NCACC Centennial)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Chair read a joint centennial resolution honoring the 1908 founding of the North Carolina Association of County Commissioners (NCACC), noting that NCACC is led by Executive Director David Thompson, Durham's former county manager in the late 1990s. The Board unanimously adopted the resolution for signature by all commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Triangle Business Journal Space Awards Recognition (Quintiles Expansion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners highlighted an award received at the Triangle Business Journal Space Awards banquet alongside Ted Conner of the Chamber of Commerce and Vivian Powell of the North Carolina Department of Commerce. The award recognized the Quintiles expansion as the most significant commercial real estate project in the Triangle for an existing industry.

agenda_items.title: Design With Brick Honor Award (North Regional Branch Library)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized the North Regional Branch Library, completed the prior year, for receiving a Design With Brick Honor Award, with Azena Howard from the Freelon architectural firm addressing the Board before the transcript was truncated.

agenda_items.title: Deferred Residential Development / Zoning Application (Pre-Item 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a gap in the transcript digest, commissioners debated a residential development project's carrying costs, sewer line infrastructure, clubhouse-level parking, two-car garages hidden from street view, and whether the Board was dismissing the Planning and Zoning Commission's recommendation. The Board voted 4-1 to defer the item for two weeks, with Commissioner Becky M. Heron dissenting.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Plan Amendment A0717 (Hebron Road Elementary School)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented county-initiated Comprehensive Plan Amendment A0717 at Hebron Road and Old Oxford Highway to redesignate 58 western acres (inventoried natural areas) from Industrial to Recreation Open Space and 25 eastern acres (purchased by Durham County for a future elementary school) from Industrial to Institutional. Staff and the Planning Commission (13-0 on January 8, 2008) recommended approval, and no citizens spoke at the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Plan Amendment A0716 (Page Road Corporate Center)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Plan Amendment A0716 for 36.48 acres north and west of Page Road in the Urban Tier to change the future land use designation from Medium Density Residential (6-12 units/acre) to Office as a transition between nearby residential areas and Imperial Center office/industrial uses. Applicant representative Bob Somal spoke in support, noting zero school impact and increased tax base alongside the Planning Commission's 13-0 recommendation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Adoption of Two-Thirds General Obligation Bond Orders
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney introduced the public hearing for three two-thirds general obligation bond orders, with no citizens speaking during the hearing. In three separate unanimous votes, the Board authorized $500,000 in library facility bonds, $4,950,000 in public building bonds, and $6,650,000 in school bonds before welcoming the County Manager back and adjourning at 9:35 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Chair Ellen W. Reckhow absent and excused, Michael D. Page presided over the February 11, 2008 regular session, where commissioners recognized Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau CEO Shelley Green's DMAP board appointment, a MADD volunteer award, and two state awards earned by The Durham Center. On the consent agenda, the Board unanimously (4-0) approved items A, C, D, E, F, G, I, and J, and after public comment from Victoria Peterson unanimously (4-0) approved Item H ($287,085 Duke University grant establishing 12 FTEs for the Durham Connects postpartum home visiting program) and Item K (three-year Johnston Ambulance Service franchise renewal). On pulled Consent Item B, a $646,275 architectural design contract with DTW Architects and Planners for renovating Durham County Memorial Stadium, the Board split 3-1: Becky M. Heron, Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr., and Michael D. Page voted Aye to invest in the stadium for increased community use, while Lewis A. Cheek voted Nay, citing Shaw University's withdrawal and arguing the project was not the best use of county funds or property. The Board concluded by unanimously (4-0) approving first reading of $12,100,000 in two-thirds bond orders, receiving the sworn statement of debt, and setting a February 25, 2008 public hearing.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the Pledge of Allegiance, a commissioner reported on an NCACC taxation committee meeting and potential annexation/homestead legislative issues. Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. moved (with a second) to excuse absent Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, with commissioners noting they had already excused her at the work session, and announced a Wednesday 7:00 p.m. Transportation Improvement Program public hearing with City Council.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered minutes from the December 20, 2007 joint BOCC/City Council meeting and the January 14 and January 28, 2008 regular sessions. Commissioners noted a clarification on page 15 of the January 14 minutes regarding creating a housing support team for homeless individuals and families before approving the minutes 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions: Shelley Green (DMAP), MADD Volunteer Award, and The Durham Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners recognized Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau CEO Shelley Green on her three-year appointment to the international Board of Directors for the Destination Marketing Accreditation Program (DMAP), and presented a MADD civic award to volunteer Sarah for monthly victim impact panels. The Durham Center was also recognized for winning an Excellence in Best Practice award (cutting institutional stays from 6.8 to 1.1 days per 90-day period) and a Public Awareness and Advocacy award for Durham Recovery Culture.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A, C, D, E, F, G, I, and J)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the unpulled consent agenda items: a $146,330 DSS One Source document imaging contract amendment (total NTE $305,755); resolutions setting March 10, 2008 public hearings to close East Institute Drive (SC07-09) and Hames Drive (SC07-07); City-County Appearance Commission interlocal agreement revision; Social Services budget amendment #08BCC00058 recognizing $472,946 in state/federal grants; advertising 2007 tax liens in March; and a school facilities reimbursement resolution tied to $194,240,000 in school bonds.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item B: Durham County Memorial Stadium Renovation Design Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek pulled Item B ($489,500 basic services plus $156,775 additional/reimbursable expenses, totaling $646,275 with DTW Architects and Planners for Durham County Memorial Stadium renovations), arguing it was a poor use of county funds and property after Shaw University withdrew its participation agreement. Supporters countered that the upgrades would make the stadium a premier county facility attracting new user proposals, and the contract passed 3-1.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item H: Budget Amendment #08BCC0059 (Durham Connects Home Visiting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item H ($287,085 from Duke University Center for Child and Family Policy to implement the Durham Connects postpartum home visiting program and establish 12.0 FTEs: one PHN Supervisor I, one Processing Assistant III, and ten PHN IIs), raising concerns about home visitors reporting maltreatment and foster care placements. Commissioners voiced strong support for the program concept and approved the item 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item K: Johnston Ambulance Service Three-Year Franchise Renewal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson also pulled Item K, asking about Johnston Ambulance Service's client breakdown between Durham and Orange counties and total revenue generated. After staff/applicant confirmation that operations were in good order, the Board approved the three-year franchise renewal 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Introduction and First Reading of Two-Thirds General Obligation Bond Orders
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Chuck Kitchen explained the first reading process for two-thirds general obligation bond orders totaling $12,100,000 ($500,000 library facilities, $4,950,000 public buildings, and $6,650,000 school bonds) following Local Government Commission application filing. The Board unanimously approved first reading, received the sworn statement of debt, and set the public hearing for February 25, 2008 before adjourning at 7:40 p.m.

votes.notes: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow was absent/excused; note at February 25 meeting a commissioner requested checking page 13 of the February 11 minutes regarding Item H's mover/seconder.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 28, 2008 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners recognized the Budget Management Services Department for its fourth consecutive GFOA Distinguished Budget Presentation Award and honored former Tax Administrator Kenneth Joyner for five years of service. The Board unanimously (5-0) approved the January 7, 2008 work session minutes and the consent agenda, including multiple public health grants, a $229,470 detention center expansion master planning contract, Justice Center geotechnical evaluation and Southwest Branch Library design amendments, and a $227,753 EMS/fire ambulance replacement contract. Following a deferral request on Items 11 and 12 and a middle transcript gap, commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved a comprehensive plan amendment dividing northern and southern tracts between Low-Medium Density Residential and Commercial designations, a technical UDO conservation subdivision text change (Section 6.2.4), and an NCDOT FY 2008–2009 Community Transportation Grant application. On second reading following public testimony from homeless residents and advocates, the Board unanimously (5-0) adopted the ordinance regulating street and highway solicitation effective July 1, 2008, and after a closed session unanimously (5-0) authorized conservation easement purchase options on 75 acres of Roger Tilly Farm and 300 acres of Frank Farm.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Deferral Scheduling for Items 11 and 12
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow noted a deferral request on Items 11 and 12 to allow time to resolve outstanding issues and stated the Board would address the deferral immediately after the consent agenda so attendees would not have to wait.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 7, 2008 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the minutes of the January 7, 2008 work session without modification.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions: GFOA Distinguished Budget Award and Kenneth Joyner
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager and Budget Director Pam Myers (with budget staff) accepted Durham County's fourth consecutive Government Finance Officers Association Distinguished Budget Presentation Award for FY 2007–08, noting commissioners' budget season starts May 27. The Board also recognized former Tax Administrator Kenneth Joyner for five years of service during which the county's tax collection rate steadily rose.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Public Health Grants, Capital & Contract Amendments)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved consent items including December 2007 tax releases/refunds; public health grant amendments ($12,000 Healthy Carolinians, $112,647 Ryan White Part C, $20,000 preparedness, $833 Title X, $10,000 Kate B. Reynolds, $4,080 tobacco prevention); $650,000 tax revenue recognition (Turner Business Appraisers); closing 6 DPS projects and reserving $234,412 unspent bond proceeds; $227,753 EMS/Redwood VFD ambulance contract; $18,394.70 Justice Center geotechnical amendment; $18,000 Southwest Branch Library design amendment; $229,470 O'Brien Atkins detention center master planning contract (plus $100,000 NTE related contracts); Johnston Ambulance franchise first reading; and a under-$30,000 architectural/engineering exemption resolution (with one amendment noted as deferred).

agenda_items.title: Deferral Request by ECON Communities (Patrick Byker)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Patrick Byker, representing ECON/FCON Communities, requested a two-cycle continuance of the public hearings on Items 11 and 12 to resolve outstanding matters with the Planning Director. Chair Reckhow encouraged the developer to examine density options before the transcript was truncated.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (truncated prior to vote)

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment: Northern and Southern Tracts Land Use Designation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle transcript gap, commissioners finalized motion language converting the northern tract to Low-Medium Density Residential, converting only the four RS-20 residential parcels on the southern tract from Commercial to Low-Medium Density Residential, and retaining the residual CG-zoned tract in the Commercial designation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change – Conservation Subdivision Technical Standards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin presented a technical text amendment to UDO Section 6.2.4 clarifying that purpose and open space intent provisions serve as explicit evaluation standards under recent state subdivision legislation, ahead of broader conservation subdivision revisions expected in March. The Planning Commission recommended approval 12-0 on December 11, 2007, and no speakers signed up for the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: NCDOT FY 2008–2009 Community Transportation Grant Application
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Johnny Ford presented the county's FY 2008–2009 North Carolina Department of Transportation Community Transportation Grant application request. No citizens signed up to speak after the public hearing opened, and the Board approved the application 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Second Reading: Regulation of Solicitation on Streets and Highways of Durham County
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board held a second reading of the street and highway solicitation ordinance because the prior vote had not been unanimous. Speakers including Scott Ritone, Jay Davis, and unhoused residents testified about survival needs, median solicitation, and access to mental health and housing assistance; commissioners noted Durham Center and housing staff were present to connect individuals to services and adopted the ordinance 5-0 effective July 1, 2008.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Conservation Easement Options (Tilly Farm and Frank Farm)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(5) to consult with counsel and instruct staff on property acquisitions involving McClendon (7408 Big Horn Drive), Frank (2306 Moores Mill Road), Tilly (1811 Tilly Farm Road), and AIDS Community Residence (4404 Guess Road). Returning to open session, the Board unanimously approved options to purchase conservation easements on 75 acres of Roger Tilly Farm and 300 acres of Frank Farm before adjourning at 10:06 p.m.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 14, 2008 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners added a Local Emergency Planning Committee roster item, excused a commissioner from the January 28 meeting, approved amended December 3 work session minutes, and presented a resolution honoring the 2008 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. commemorative events. Commissioners unanimously (5-0) adopted Consent Agenda Items A–H—including eliminating library meeting room fees for nonprofits, adopting the new Minority and Women Business Enterprise (MWBE) Ordinance, establishing 10 provisional Social Services shell positions, and approving a Durham Public Schools annexation petition for New Elementary B—while correcting the Medicare Part D contract end date to December 31, 2008. After a middle transcript gap covering the Economic Development Policy resolution, the Board unanimously (5-0) approved a transportation Special Use Permit with traffic mitigation conditions and a major site plan/preliminary plat for 369 single-family and 130 townhome lots on a 422.6-acre PDR 3.0 tract in the Falls/Jordan watershed. Finally, the Board unanimously (5-0) approved $66,946 in Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) matching grants and the updated Local Emergency Planning Committee membership roster and quarterly schedule with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Addition, Announcements, and January 28 Excusal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow added a Local Emergency Planning Committee roster action to the end of the agenda and announced Durham Neighborhood College spring applications (due January 18), a January 29 NCDOT Hopson Road (SR 1978) grade separation workshop, and Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee recruitment. The Board unanimously approved excusing a commissioner from the January 28 meeting, and a commissioner recapped the Mount Sinai Baptist Church prayer breakfast.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (December 3 Work Session Vote Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an amendment to the December 3 work session minutes correcting the recorded vote for election of Chair and Vice Chair to match actual proceedings, along with a minor word-duplication fix. The Board approved the minutes unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting 2008 Events Honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read a resolution honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. events held January 18–21, 2008 (marking the 40th anniversary of his passing), including the march from North Carolina Mutual Life Insurance Company to First Presbyterian Church and culmination at Union Baptist Church, and presented it to Doris Ingram and committee members. Commissioners also announced Marian Wright Edelman's January 20 Duke Chapel address and the City-County employee MLK service.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A–H: MWBE Ordinance, Library Fees, DPS Annexation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved Consent Agenda Items A–H: acceptance of a Friends of the Durham Library storage shed; 2008 Medicare Part D employer list bill (term corrected to December 31, 2008); $19,056 fund balance appropriation for Juvenile Crime Prevention Council reimbursement; $23,016 Library Foundation gift recognition for technology; elimination of library meeting room fees for nonprofits ($25 refreshment / $100 commercial fees retained); 10 provisional Social Services shell positions from lapsed salaries; the county's new MWBE Ordinance effective January 14, 2008; and a DPS annexation petition for New Elementary B.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Adopting Economic Development Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow introduced the Economic Development Policy developed over six months under the County Manager's work plan with input from Durham CAN, the Chamber of Commerce, and Downtown Durham Inc., before the transcript was truncated for size.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (truncated prior to vote)

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Hearing: Transportation Special Use Permit Order
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle transcript gap, the Board considered a draft order granting a transportation Special Use Permit incorporating a full list of traffic mitigation conditions recommended by staff, NCDOT, and the Transportation Department (also accounting for a future un-rezoned phase in the TIA). Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek noted approving the order secured the strongest available traffic mitigation protections, and the Board approved it 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Major Site Plan and Preliminary Plat (369 Single-Family & 130 Townhome Lots)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Terry Diner) presented a major site plan and preliminary plat for 369 single-family and 130 townhome lots with a pool, clubhouse, and tennis courts on 176.36 acres of a 422.6-acre PDR 3.0 site in the Falls/Jordan protected area and Neuse Basin, recommended for approval by staff and DRB. Commissioners discussed mulch trails near hunting/Army Corps boundaries, the county ordinance prohibiting firearm discharge within 600 feet of a residence, tree protection fencing for mass grading buffers, and the developer's $500-per-unit school donation before approving 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST) Commission Matching Grants
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget analyst Kevin Etheridge presented the 2007–08 DOST matching grants recommendations (from an $85,000 budget and $169,945 in requests), recommending $66,946 across projects including Asbury Methodist Preschool playground ($13,824), Central Park School equipment ($31,132), and Durham-Orange Recreational Disc Golf Association ($21,390). One commissioner questioned spending $21,390 on a disc golf course before noting they would support the committee's thorough review, and the Board approved the grants 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Added Item: Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC) Membership and Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow presented a time-sensitive letter from the Local Emergency Planning Committee requesting approval of an updated membership roster and a switch to quarterly meetings in the upcoming year. The Board unanimously approved the roster and schedule before adjourning at 10:35 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 10, 2007 regular session, Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek announced a December 13 press conference to address public questions about his meeting absences and highlighted a statewide study ranking Durham as the third safest large city in North Carolina. The Board received a holiday thank-you presentation from the Eno River Association, adopted and read the annual Bill of Rights Defense Resolution on Human Rights Day, recognized Sheriff's Office, Emergency Management, and State Highway Patrol personnel for a life-saving Falls Lake rescue, and heard a 2008 revaluation update from outgoing Tax Administrator Ken Joyner. Commissioners also debated NCDOT's planned Hillendale Road widening project ahead of a January comment deadline, with a commissioner advocating a five-lane center turn lane over NCDOT's proposed 17.5-foot raised grass median while City Transportation staff defended the median's safety and pedestrian benefits. In formal action, the Board unanimously (5-0) approved three sets of minutes, entered closed session for the County Manager's performance evaluation, and unanimously (5-0) set County Manager Michael M. Ruffin's salary at $170,000, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Commissioner Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the meeting and recognized Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek, who announced a Thursday press conference regarding his meeting absences and continued service and cited crime statistics ranking Durham third safest among large North Carolina municipalities behind Cary and Raleigh. Commissioners also noted a domestic violence vigil co-sponsored by Delta Sigma Theta Sorority and the Durham County Women's Commission, as well as a recent NCACC briefing in Raleigh on new local transportation improvement legislation.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow noted two minor typographical corrections to the November 12 and November 26, 2007 minutes (correcting 'Casey Steinbacher' and 'vibrant'). Commissioners approved the three sets of minutes as corrected.

agenda_items.title: Eno River Association Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Eno River Association Executive Director Robin Jacobs and Director of Land Protection Clay Jordan thanked the Board for its partnership on land conservation and open space protection, speaking alongside Triangle Land Conservancy's support for collaborative regional conservation efforts.

agenda_items.title: Bill of Rights Defense Resolution and Jail Maintenance Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow read the Board's annual Bill of Rights Defense Resolution reaffirming constitutional civil rights and liberties—originally adopted September 22, 2003—on Human Rights Day, and presented it to Durham Bill of Rights Defense Committee Chair Joan Walsh. Prior to moving on, Chair Reckhow also asked the County Manager to follow up with the Sheriff and General Services Director regarding maintenance issues at the jail.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Life-Saving Rescue for Donald Meaks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheriff Worth Hill, Emergency Management official Jeff Batten, and Major Andrews recounted the September 30 search-and-rescue response at Falls Lake that saved Donald Meaks's life during an evening with simultaneous missing-person calls. The Board recognized participating personnel from the Sheriff's Office, Durham County Emergency Management, and the North Carolina Highway Patrol Aviation Unit.

agenda_items.title: NCDOT Hillendale Road Improvement Project Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City of Durham Transportation Division engineer Wesley outlined NCDOT's Hillendale Road public hearing map and early January comment deadline. A commissioner who placed the item on the agenda cited a roughly 400-signature neighborhood petition gathered by David Bysher opposing NCDOT's 17.5-foot raised grass median, lane taper, and right-turn lane north of Carver Street in favor of a five-lane center turn lane to protect business access and trees, whereas Wesley explained that a raised median reduces vehicular conflict points and crashes and provides pedestrian refuge while median cut locations remain open to comment.

agenda_items.title: 2008 Property Revaluation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Outgoing Tax Administrator Ken Joyner reported on initial public response following the November 19 revaluation notice rollout and outlined the schedule for informal hearings beginning in January through March ahead of the Board of Equalization and Review. Chair Reckhow thanked Joyner for his leadership as he departs for the UNC Institute of Government, noting Kim Simpson will take over the office.

agenda_items.title: Joint City-County Meeting Scheduling and Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed scheduling conflicts involving Audit Committee meetings when selecting dates for a joint meeting with the Mayor and City Council. Ballot selections were also announced appointing Amanda Arrington and Evelyn Nicholson to the Animal Control Advisory Committee and Sandra E. Peele and Ronald E. Spain to the Public Health Board.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: County Manager Performance Evaluation and Salary Adjustment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to evaluate the performance of County Manager Michael M. Ruffin. Returning to open session at 02:28:58, Chair Reckhow commended the Manager for an excellent year and the Board unanimously approved setting his annual salary at $170,000 before adjourning at 9:26 p.m.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve three sets of minutes with minor typographical corrections noted by the Chair.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adjourn to closed session to evaluate the performance of a public officer/employee under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

votes.item_title: Set County Manager Salary at $170,000
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote upon return from closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the closed-session performance evaluation, the Board commended County Manager Michael M. Ruffin for his performance over the past year and voted to set his salary at $170,000.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 26, 2007 regular session, the Board recognized Vote for Learning co-chairs Mary Ann Black and Steve Tolar following the overwhelming passage of the November 6 bond referendum and honored Sheriff Worth Hill and the Durham County Sheriff's Office as a 2007 CALEA Flagship Agency. Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved a comprehensive consent agenda advancing $4.703 million from fund balance for school capital projects, expanding pretrial electronic monitoring, declaring official bond referendum results, exempting the Detention Center expansion from RFQ architect selection, and appointing Kim Simpson as Interim Tax Administrator effective January 1, 2008. Following the consent vote, Simpson and Tax Administrator Ken Joyner briefed the Board on the November 16 mailing of 97,000 revaluation notices and preliminary revenue-neutral tax rate estimates (69.2 cents for the County). In later business, the Board unanimously (5-0) directed staff regarding an NCDOT item requiring action by December 10, adopted a technical metes-and-bounds correction for zoning Case Z05-33, approved Unified Development Ordinance text amendment TC0704 on open space payment-in-lieu despite earlier Planning Commission deadlock, and entered closed session, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Revised Agenda, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow welcomed attendees, noted that a closed session had been added to the revised agenda, and led the approval of minutes for the October 22 regular session and November 5 work session.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions: Vote for Learning Co-Chairs and Sheriff's Office CALEA Flagship Designation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners honored Mary Ann Black and Steve Tolar for co-chairing the Vote for Learning Committee, noting school bond support rose from roughly 50% in early polling to over 75% at the November 6 election. The Board also congratulated Sheriff Worth Hill and the Durham County Sheriff's Office on being designated a 2007 Flagship Agency by the Commission on Accreditation for Law Enforcement Agencies (CALEA), the seventh NC agency and only NC Sheriff's Office to receive the honor.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and 2008 Property Revaluation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved consent items including July 2007 property tax releases, a $66,144 emergency management grant, a $4,703,050 fund balance advance for DPS capital projects (reimbursable from spring 2008 GO bonds), Detention Center expansion funding and RFQ exemption, $146,723 for Criminal Justice Resource Center pretrial services and electronic monitoring, declaration of November 6 bond referendum results, a Duke Energy right-of-way agreement for Ferrell/Federal Street Elementary, declining a surplus property offer on Dashion Avenue, appointing Kim Simpson as Interim Tax Administrator ($96,870 salary), and supporting a dropout prevention grant. Afterward, Simpson and Tax Administrator Ken Joyner reported on the November 16 mailing of ~97,000 revaluation notices, appeal timelines before the Board of Equalization and Review, and revenue-neutral estimates of 69.2 cents for the County and 50.05 cents for the City.

agenda_items.title: NCDOT Consultation and December 10 Deadline Motion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, commissioners discussed meeting with NCDOT staff as soon as possible—potentially within the week—to resolve outstanding issues and bring an item back for a Board vote by December 10, 2007. Commissioners also noted dissatisfaction that Planning Commission lacked materials provided to the Board and that the County cannot force NCDOT to act on a fixed timeline.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Technical Corrections for Zoning Map Change (Case Z05-33)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planner Scott Whiteman presented a technical correction to the July 24, 2006 ordinance for Case Z05-33 after an annexation petition uncovered a discrepancy in the attached metes-and-bounds legal description. Whiteman confirmed the correction makes the prior zoning valid without changing the zoning designation or adopted development plan, noting a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation; no members of the public spoke.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change TC0704 (Open Space Payment in Lieu)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Julia Mullen presented UDO text amendment TC0704, allowing qualifying small developments to make a payment in lieu of open space (spent within the same recreation district) to avoid creating homeowners associations, and allowing tree coverage areas on private lots for developments without buffers. Commissioner Becky M. Heron questioned how tree coverage on private lots would be protected against clearing after sale, and Mullen noted the Planning Commission had recommended denial 6-6 on that issue; with no public speakers, the Board approved the motion unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners submitted ballots for board and commission vacancies, resulting in appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Board (Gregory Barno), Civic Center Authority, Open Space and Trails Commission (Charles Welch), Women's Commission (Stacy Robinson), and Workforce Development Board. Chair Reckhow also reminded commissioners that the upcoming Monday work session would run from 9:00 a.m. to as late as 3:00 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Personnel Fitness and Litigation (County of Durham v. AREC 3 LLC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) regarding the fitness of a public officer/employee and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding attorney-client privilege in County of Durham v. AREC 3 LLC / AROC 6 (06 CVS 847). Upon returning to open session at 02:34:50, the Board reported giving direction to staff with no action taken and adjourned at 9:39 p.m.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 12, 2007 regular session, Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek returned to the Board and stated he was consulting with his physicians and would address public questions about his attendance and service in the future. Commissioners presented two North Carolina Social Services best-practice awards, proclaimed November as Hire a Veteran Month and recognized American Education Week, and read a lengthy consent agenda featuring a Wackenhut building security contract, Judicial Building security upgrades, and multiple public health grants (with the consent vote itself falling inside a truncated transcript gap). Tax Administrator Ken Joyner delivered a detailed preview of the November 16 mailing of 2008 revaluation notices—showing the County real property base rising from $18.075 billion to over $23.4 billion—along with expanded 17-line call-center staffing and the January-to-May informal and formal appeals calendar. Before adjourning, commissioners discussed an earlier state/NC State presentation and directed County Manager Michael Ruffin to obtain background details and pursue a better-noticed public forum, with no formal votes captured in the visible transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Veterans Day Tribute, and Commissioner Cheek Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the meeting on Veterans Day, honored Durham County veterans, and recognized Boy Scout Troop 486 working on citizenship badges. Returning Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek thanked colleagues and supporters for their work during his absence, acknowledged questions about his attendance and service as legitimate, and stated he was consulting his physicians and would address the issue later.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Social Services Best Practice Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners noted the Neighborhood College graduation and praised the animal shelter's emergency response, noting over 250 adoption applications under review. The Board then recognized Department of Social Services Director Sammy Haithcock, Sharon Hurr, and staff for winning two North Carolina Association of County Directors of Social Services Best Practice Awards for the long-term care website and 'Investing in Human Capital' partnership series.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: Hire a Veteran Month and American Education Week
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read a proclamation declaring November as Hire a Veteran Month, accepted by Lindsay Atkins, who thanked the Chair for attending Durham's first veterans job fair on November 7. Commissioners also presented an American Education Week proclamation to Durham Association of Educators President Donald Berenger ahead of November 16 Substitute Educators Day.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read consent items A through M+, including a county building security services contract with Wackenhut Corporation, donation of a surplus ambulance van to Bahama/Bare Pond Volunteer Fire Department, relocation of the Shaw Family Cemetery, a $63,685 Judicial Building and Annex security upgrade contract with TAC Carolinas, a Chapter 24 parking ordinance amendment, a $14,659 Sheriff's Office BJA grant, a $75,000 tax service amendment, and several public health grants (lead poisoning prevention, risk reduction, women's health/TANF pregnancy prevention, TV/radio health media, Project DIRECT diabetes education, and nutrition/physical activity). The consent vote occurred during a subsequent transcript truncation gap.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (vote omitted in transcript truncation)

agenda_items.title: 2008 Property Revaluation Mailing and Appeals Process Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Ken Joyner presented the November 16, 2007 mailing of revaluation notices, showing Durham County's real property tax base growing from $18.075 billion (2001 base) to over $23.4 billion and the City's from $14.059 billion to $18.739 billion. Joyner detailed expanded call-center capacity (17 phone lines, 40+ trained staff, extended hours Nov 19–Dec 19), informal reviews starting January 2, and formal Board of Equalization and Review hearings starting in May, earning praise from Commissioner Cheek for a thorough, citizen-friendly rollout.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up on State / NC State Project Presentation and Public Forum

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 22, 2007 regular session, the Board approved three sets of minutes (5-0), issued proclamations for Adoption Awareness Month and In-Home Health/Hospice Services, and forwarded a signed Climate Change Mitigation Resolution to NACo committing county government operations to a 50% greenhouse gas reduction from 2005 levels by 2030 alongside a joint Sustainability Manager. Following a mid-meeting truncation gap, commissioners discussed water and sewer constraints on development during a zoning map change hearing and unanimously (5-0) approved the rezoning request. The Board also unanimously (5-0) approved County Manager Michael Ruffin's recommendation to transition employee medical coverage from the NCACC/Cigna pool—which had proposed a 14.3% increase—to an 18-month Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina contract effective January 1, 2008 to align benefits with the fiscal year while keeping NCACC dental coverage. Commissioners referred a Design District Review Team appointment back to JCCPC, announced several board appointments, and voted 5-0 to enter closed session on personnel and tax/litigation matters, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners announced an Animal Protection Society Halloween fundraiser at Camp Bow Wow on Page Road, Kids Voting volunteer recruitment through Cooperative Extension, and a November 3 community Health Summit at the Durham Civic Center. The Board then unanimously approved three sets of minutes with minor technical corrections.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Recognitions: Adoption Month, Home Health/Hospice, Climate Change Resolution, and Wastewater Gold Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Michael D. Page read the Adoption Awareness Month proclamation noting 23+ Durham County children awaiting adoption, accepted by Social Services Director Sammy Haithcock and staff, followed by an In-Home Health, Hospice, and Community-Based Services proclamation. Under Item 8, Chair Reckhow read a signed Resolution to Reduce the Risk of Climate Change for submission to NACo—committing county operations to a 50% greenhouse gas cut from 2005 levels by 2030 and hiring a joint City-County Sustainability Manager—and under Item 9 recognized the Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant's NACWA Performance Gold Award.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, commissioners questioned developers and staff about drought and water-capacity implications for a proposed rezoning, noting the requested density was lower than current zoning and that the City of Durham controls water and sewer hookups at build-out. After closing the public hearing, the Board voted unanimously to approve the zoning map change.

agenda_items.title: Employee Health and Dental Benefits Transition to Blue Cross Blue Shield
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Michael Ruffin and staff reported that the NCACC/Cigna pool quoted a 14.3% medical renewal increase for 2008 versus the 10% budgeted for 1,800+ employees. Staff recommended switching medical benefits to Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina (using MedCo for deeper prescription discounts) on an 18-month contract from January 1, 2008 through June 30, 2009 to align future renewals with the fiscal year, separating ABC employees, and retaining NCACC dental coverage while a commissioner urged future study of self-insurance.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow and Commissioner Heron referred a Design District Review Team appointment back to JCCPC for re-advertisement because the applicant was a city employee. Ballot selections were announced for the Animal Control Review Board, Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau / Tourism Development Authority, Durham County Hospital Corporation, Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee (Greg Reed), Raleigh-Durham Noise Abatement Committee, and Transportation Advisory Board (Joseph Kilshoff).

meetings.executive_summary: With Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek excused (4-0) on October 8, 2007, the Board voted 4-0 to defer Item 16 (street and highway solicitation/panhandling ordinance) and refer it to the Joint City-County Committee, with Commissioners Becky M. Heron and Michael D. Page emphasizing that most panhandling occurs inside city limits and requires City collaboration. Commissioners honored youth Jose Diaz for heroism in rescuing his grandmother and saving his home from fire, unanimously (4-0) approved Consent Items 6A–6D (Memorial Stadium deal points, EMS vehicle exhaust contract, Sheriff's GREAT grant, and surplus property sales), and heard Heron's procedural objection to pulled Item 6E ($100,000 City of Medicine Academy lease) before a mid-meeting truncation. Later, the Board voted 4-0 to approve a UDO text amendment, granted Transportation Special Use Permit Case T06-01 and the Major Site Plan for The Worship Center at Lumley and Page Roads (4-0 each), adopted a resolution supporting the Camp Butner Joint Land Use Study and appointing Chair Ellen W. Reckhow (4-0), and entered closed session (4-0), with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Commissioner Cheek, and Deferral of Item 16 (Solicitation Ordinance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 4-0 to excuse absent Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek and wished him a quick recovery. Citing Cheek's absence and observations by Commissioners Becky M. Heron and Michael D. Page that panhandling overwhelmingly occurs within city limits, the Board voted 4-0 to defer Item 16 (regulating solicitation on county streets and highways) and refer it to the Joint City-County Committee, while apologizing to citizens attending for the item.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow announced the October 10 bond campaign kickoff for DPS, Durham Tech, and Museum of Life and Science bonds, an October 10 Transportation Improvement Plan public hearing, and the next day's City Council primary election, while Commissioner Page shared a DSS announcement. Commissioners then approved two sets of minutes (including September 10 with a typo correction) by a 4-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Heroism: Jose Diaz
agenda_items.discussion_summary: EMS Supervisor Jackie Holmes and Assistant County Manager Deborah Craig-Gray described how youth Jose Diaz came home from school on February 8 to find his grandmother incapacitated by a medical emergency while cooking and acted quickly to save her and prevent a house fire. Chair Reckhow presented Diaz with a certificate of appreciation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A–6D Approved; Item 6E Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved Items 6A–6D: Memorial Stadium renovation business deal points, a $108,304 EMS vehicle exhaust system contract, a $47,950 Sheriff's Office 2007 GREAT gang-resistance grant, and sales of seven county surplus properties including 812 S. Roxboro Street to Self-Help CDC. On pulled Item 6E ($100,000 general fund balance appropriation for a City of Medicine Academy lease with DPS), Commissioner Heron voiced concern that such funding requests should come through a work session first, prior to a transcript truncation gap.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Technical Text Amendment (Merge Stacking)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle truncation gap, staff concluded a brief presentation on a technical UDO text amendment regarding drive-through/merge stacking. Chair Reckhow opened and closed the public hearing with no speakers, and the Board approved the amendment 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Public Hearing: Transportation Special Use Permit (Case T06-01, The Worship Center)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Witnesses and staff were sworn in for quasi-judicial Case T06-01 for The Worship Center at Lumley and Page Roads. Planner Michael Stock presented staff findings and required road improvements (a northbound left-turn lane, southbound right-turn lane, and three-lane site drive on Page Road), Commissioner Heron queried whether signalization at Lumley and Page took future church traffic into account, and the Board approved the draft order 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Major Site Plan: The Worship Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Planning Director Steve Medlin presented the Major Site Plan for The Worship Center. Commissioners confirmed the facility could not be used as a school without separate approvals, reviewed health/facility requirements and retention of existing landscaped buffers, and approved the site plan 4-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Planning Director Steve Medlin presented the North Carolina National Guard's Camp Butner Joint Land Use Study covering 4,940 acres in northeastern Durham County. Chair Ellen W. Reckhow volunteered to serve on the study policy committee, Commissioner Heron noted strong concern among northern Durham residents about a proposed facility there, and the Board adopted the supporting resolution and appointed Reckhow by a 4-0 vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 24, 2007 regular session, County Manager Michael Ruffin introduced Steve Medlin as Interim City-County Planning Director following Frank Duke's departure, and the Board recognized 4-H lifetime volunteer award recipient Betsy Chandler Vatuik and issued a Minority and Women Business Enterprise proclamation. Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved the September 4 work session minutes and all consent items (6A, 6C–6F, 6H–6J), and separately approved (5-0) pulled Item 6B (auctioneer contract with Jerry L. Harris after inquiring about online government auctions) and pulled Item 6G (a Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant reclaimed-water engineering contract amendment with Camp Dresser & McKee to develop rate structures ahead of interlocal agreements with Cary and Wake County). Vote for Learning co-chairs Mary Ann Black and Steve Tolar presented an overview of the $207.1 million November 6 general obligation bond package for Durham Public Schools ($194.24 million), Durham Tech ($8.68 million), and the Museum of Life and Science ($4.18 million), after which the Board announced ballot appointments to six advisory bodies and adjourned with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Interim Planning Director Introduction, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Michael Ruffin introduced 25-year planner Steve Medlin as Interim City-County Planning Director following Frank Duke's September 21 departure. Commissioners also announced an NCDOT design public hearing on South Miami Boulevard (comment period through October 24) and upcoming Animal Protection Society dog-wash, shelter open-house, and Halloween events.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (September 4, 2007 Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow presented the September 4, 2007 work session minutes for approval with no changes noted. The Board approved the minutes unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Recognitions and Proclamations: 4-H Volunteer Award and MWBE Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Director Delphine Sellers joined the Board in honoring Betsy Chandler Vatuik as winner of the 2007 National 4-H Salute to Excellence Outstanding Lifetime Volunteer Award. Chair Reckhow also read a proclamation recognizing Durham County's Minority and Women Business Enterprise (MWBE) nondiscrimination policy and upcoming outreach events.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A, 6C–6F, 6H–6J) and Pulled Items 6B & 6G
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved Items 6A, 6C–6F, and 6H–6J covering August tax releases/refunds, surplus property sales and upset-bid proceedings, sole-source Sheriff 800 MHz radio and Motorola Centracom console upgrades, a $5,000 Welcome Baby adjustment, and advisory appointments. On pulled Item 6B (public auctioneer contract with Jerry L. Harris), Purchasing Manager Jacqueline Boyce explained staff was still evaluating online auction platforms while offering surplus vans to nonprofits; on pulled Item 6G (Camp Dresser & McKee contract amendment for Triangle WWTP reclaimed water), staff briefed the Board on 60%-complete Durham County designs, coordination with Cary and Wake County, a $2.3 million EPA grant, and rate-study work needed prior to RTP customer connections. Both pulled items passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Overview of November 6, 2007 Bond Campaign ($207.1 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vote for Learning co-chairs Mary Ann Black and Steve Tolar presented the $207.1 million general obligation bond referendum on the November 6 ballot—comprising $194,240,000 for Durham Public Schools, $8,680,000 for Durham Technical Community College, and $4,180,000 for the Museum of Life and Science—and invited commissioners to the October 10 community kickoff. Commissioners praised the balanced distribution across former city and county schools, including a $1.6 million gymnasium for Lakeview Alternative School and secondary education investments.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ballot selections were announced for the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Board, Community Child Protection / Child Fatality Prevention Team, Criminal Justice Partnership Advisory Board, Multi-Jurisdictional Advisory Board, Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee, and Triangle J Water Resources Committee, while Chair Reckhow advised commissioners to reserve mid-afternoon time for longer November and December work sessions before adjourning at 8:00 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (August 27, 2007 Regular Session)
