meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 27, 2007 regular session, the Board approved three sets of minutes (5-0), honored Durham Center Lifetime Leadership Award recipient Vivian Harris, and proclaimed September as Alcohol and Drug Addiction Recovery Month. Commissioners unanimously (5-0) approved Consent Items 7A–7H and 7J—including Library and Audit Oversight bylaws updates, a $5 detention DVD/CD fee, a 45.3-acre Poole Farm conservation easement substitution ($200,500), and a $605,760 Triangle WWTP sludge contract—and separately approved (5-0) pulled Item 7I (ECS Carolinas geotechnical testing for the proposed Justice Center) subject to County Attorney approval. Under Item 8, County Manager Michael Ruffin recommended against placing either the 0.25% local sales tax or 0.4% land transfer tax on the November 2007 ballot—citing declining bond support, organized opposition from the People's Alliance and Realtors, and insufficient public dialogue—and commissioners agreed to focus on the November bond package while developing a citizen-committee framework for future revenue discussions. The Board concluded with ballot appointments, a closed session on County of Durham v. Day (5-0), and adjournment with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow noted an amendment to Consent Item 7I adding County Attorney approval and celebrated the festive reopening of Durham County Stadium with $90,000 in short-term improvements and Shaw University's marching band and football team. The Board then approved three sets of minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Vivian Harris and Substance Abuse Recovery Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Alongside Durham Center Director Ellen Holloman, the Board recognized longtime employee Vivian Harris for winning the 2007 North Carolina Council of Community Programs Lifetime Leadership Award. Commissioners also proclaimed September as Alcohol and Drug Addiction Recovery Month, with Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek emphasizing the need for sustained year-round community recovery support.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (7A–7H, 7J) and Pulled Item 7I (Justice Center Geotechnical Testing)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved Items 7A–7H and 7J, including July tax releases, Library Board bylaws, a $5 detention DVD/CD copy fee, a Little River Regional Park MOU, surplus land sales, a $200,500 Poole Farm conservation easement substitution, a $605,760 Bio-Nomic sludge contract, $43,119 returned from Correct Care Solutions, and Audit Oversight Committee bylaws (after speaker Alan Lang raised quarterly meeting and attendance questions on 7J). On pulled Item 7I, staff confirmed geotechnical contractor ECS Carolinas LLP was not the firm involved in prior jail foundation issues, and the Board approved the contract 5-0 subject to County Attorney approval.

agenda_items.title: Local Option Sales Tax (0.25%) and Land Transfer Tax (0.4%) Ballot Decision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ahead of an end-of-August Board of Elections deadline for the November ballot, County Manager Michael Ruffin recommended against putting either newly authorized tax on the November ballot, citing polling showing school bond support dropping from 49.9% to 45.4%, expected opposition from People's Alliance (sales tax) and Realtors (land transfer tax), risk of tying the bonds 'at the hip' to a tax measure, and the need for deeper community debate beyond one public hearing. Commissioners agreed—voicing opposition to a regressive sales tax, noting the soft real estate market, questioning Realtors' opposition to a 0.4% transfer fee compared to 6% sales commissions, and directing the Manager to propose a structured citizen-engagement framework at a future work session.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners thanked Assistant County Manager Deborah Craig-Gray for advancing the county's legislative agenda and announced ballot appointments to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee (Kathy Hans, Virginia Martin), Planning Commission (Linda Hough), and Workforce Development Board.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: County of Durham v. Day (03 CVS 457)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with counsel regarding County of Durham v. Day (03 CVS 457). Upon returning at 01:19:58, the Board reported no action was taken and adjourned at 8:27 p.m.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (Three Sets)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to approve three sets of minutes as distributed.

votes.item_title: Item 7I: Consulting Services Agreement with ECS Carolinas LLP (Justice Center Geotechnical Testing)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved consulting agreement with ECS Carolinas LLP for additional geotechnical testing at the proposed Durham County Justice Center site, subject to County Attorney approval, after confirming ECS Carolinas was not involved in earlier jail construction issues.

votes.item_title: Closed Session Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) (County of Durham v. Day)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to enter closed session to preserve attorney-client privilege and discuss County of Durham v. Day (03 CVS 457).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 13, 2007 regular session, the Board recognized Tax Collections employee Mary Ingram with the July Anchor Award for helping lift the county's collection rate to 98.74% and unanimously (5-0) approved the consent agenda—including the 2008 Revaluation Schedule of Values, a $50,000 Lincoln Community Health Center renovation appropriation, and a $360,000 school capital shift to Northern High School paving. Commissioners also voted 5-0 to approve the FY2007-08 Rural Operating Assistance Program (ROAP) transit grant application after requesting broader outreach to rural churches and Ruritan clubs, and heard City-County Planning Director Frank Duke present UDO floodplain fill revisions before a middle transcript gap. In Item 9's heavily attended public hearing on the newly authorized 0.25% sales tax or 0.4% land transfer tax, speakers opposed the sales tax as regressive and Realtors and preservationists opposed the land transfer tax as narrow and cyclical, while Commissioners Becky M. Heron and Michael D. Page stressed Durham's heavy property-tax burden and upcoming debt needs ahead of continued discussion on August 27, with no split votes recorded.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and July Anchor Award Recognition (Mary Ingram)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow distributed a survey for a joint meeting with the City Council and introduced Tax Administrator Ken Joyner to honor collections employee Mary Ingram as the July Anchor Award winner. Ingram was recognized for nearly a decade of service, collecting $15 million over two fiscal years and helping raise the countywide collection rate to 98.74% (and real property collections above 99%).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (2008 Schedule of Values, Health Trust, and School Capital)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved consent items including a 4-H substance abuse prevention grant from the Durham ABC Board, the 2008 Revaluation Schedule of Values and rules, Chair Reckhow's appointment as NCACC voting delegate, an upset-bid surplus property sale, a Dixon Hughes PLLC sales tax refund audit contract, $50,000 from the Community Health Trust Fund for Lincoln Community Health Center renovations, and shifting $360,000 from Northern High School HVAC to Northern High School paving.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY2007-08 Rural Operating Assistance Program (ROAP) Grant Application
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Delphine Sellers and Johnny Ford presented the consolidated FY2007-08 NCDOT ROAP application covering Elderly & Disabled, Rural General Public, and Work First Transitional Assistance ($8,415), with allocations recommended by the Transportation Advisory Board. Commissioners verified service coverage in rural areas including Bahama, asked staff to add rural churches and Ruritan clubs to outreach distribution lists, and approved the application 5-0 after closing the public hearing with no speakers.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change — Floodplain Fill and Related Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning Director Frank Duke presented federal/state technical updates and three substantive UDO revisions: requiring a major special use permit for most floodplain fill (removing Board of Adjustment variance authority), permitting the floodplain administrator to approve fill for single-family/duplex lots of record or floodproofing in lieu of fill, and authorizing Development Review Board approval for utility/stream crossing fill, all recommended 12-0 by the Planning Commission. Subsequent hearing testimony and the vote were omitted in the transcript truncation gap.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (vote omitted in transcript truncation)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Local Option Sales Tax (0.25%) vs. Land Transfer Tax (0.4%)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In a public hearing on revenue options newly authorized under Session Law 2007-323, speakers including Stephanie Hopkins opposed the quarter-cent sales tax as regressive while urging broader public education before any ballot vote, whereas the NC Association of Realtors President-Elect and Preservation Durham opposed the 0.4% land transfer tax as volatile, concentrated on ~1% of residents, and harmful to first-time buyers, seniors, and historic home rehabbers. The County Attorney confirmed state law allows no local exemptions beyond governmental units, and Commissioners Becky M. Heron and Michael D. Page emphasized Durham's reliance on property taxes ($2.3 million per penny) for school, jail, human services, and courthouse projects before continuing deliberation to August 27.

votes.item_title: FY2007-08 Rural Operating Assistance Program (ROAP) Grant Application to NCDOT
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved consolidated FY2007-08 ROAP transit grant application to NCDOT following a public hearing with no speakers.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. excused (4-0) on July 23, 2007, the Board honored late former Chief Deputy Sheriff and Chief Magistrate Chester 'Chet' Dobies and unanimously (4-0) approved Consent Items 7A–7G and 7I–7N, including $3.52 million in FY2008 capital appropriations and a $25,000 Durham History Museum allocation. On pulled Consent Item 7H—advancing $4.5 million from General Fund balance for Durham County Memorial Stadium renovations—the Board split 3-1, with Ellen W. Reckhow, Becky M. Heron, and Michael D. Page voting Aye and Lewis A. Cheek voting Nay because he considered the stadium renovation a poor expenditure of funds. County Manager Michael Ruffin then introduced the three November 6 general obligation bond orders totaling $207.1 million for Durham Public Schools ($194.24 million), Durham Tech ($8.68 million), and the Museum of Life and Science ($4.18 million) prior to a transcript gap. Later, commissioners followed up on homeless and ex-offender employment concerns ahead of an August staff report and voted 4-0 to approve Tax Administrator Ken Joyner's 2006 tax settlement (reporting a 98.74% collection rate, second highest among large NC urban counties) and charge 2007 taxes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Commissioner Cousin, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 4-0 to excuse absent Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr., pulled Item 10 (a planning item) until the following month, and unanimously approved three sets of minutes (4-0).

agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolutions for Chester 'Chet' Joseph Dobies and Audit Committee Notice
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow read a Board resolution honoring the late Chester 'Chet' Joseph Dobies—sworn in as a deputy sheriff in 1979, promoted to Chief Deputy in 1987, and later Chief Magistrate—noting his key role planning the county's jail construction, followed by a Sheriff's Office resolution read by Captain Paul Martin. Chair Reckhow also welcomed a newly hired official and invited citizens with business or accounting backgrounds to apply for the Internal Audit Committee.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (7A–7G, 7I–7N) and Pulled Item 7H (Memorial Stadium $4.5M Advance)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 4-0 to approve Consent Items 7A–7G and 7I–7N, including a $193,000 tax-bill mailing contract, $25,000 for the Durham History Museum Initiative, $3,523,726 in FY2008 capital appropriations (boardroom tech, Judicial Building, Animal Control, open space, New Hope Creek, Civic Center), a $127,046 Sheriff's BJA grant, surplus property sales, and $24,757 for Bethesda and Lebanon fire districts. Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek objected to Item 7H—advancing $4.5 million from General Fund balance for Durham County Memorial Stadium renovations—as a poor expenditure of county funds, prompting the item to be pulled and approved on a 3-1 split vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: November 6, 2007 General Obligation Bond Orders ($207.1 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Michael Ruffin outlined the three bond orders proposed for separate votes and a November 6 referendum: $194,240,000 for Durham Public Schools (covering Bethesda, Club Blvd, Creekside, Easley, Glenn, R.N. Harris, Mangum, Merrick-Moore, Parkwood, E.K. Powe, Y.E. Smith, New Elementary E at Hebron/Old Oxford, and New Elementary F land acquisition), $8,680,000 for Durham Technical Community College (including Newton Building expansion), and $4,180,000 for the Museum of Life and Science. Testimony and bond order votes fell inside the subsequent transcript truncation gap.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (votes omitted in transcript truncation)

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up on Homeless Services and Ex-Offender Employment Assistance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap, commissioners and County Manager Michael Ruffin discussed connecting public commenters—including shelter advocates and an older resident struggling with repeated job rejections—to County assistance and job development resources. Chair Reckhow noted staff would deliver a comprehensive report on homeless shelter portals of entry and action plans in mid-August.

agenda_items.title: 2006 Property Tax Settlement, 2007 Tax Charge, and Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Ken Joyner reported Durham County achieved a 98.74% FY2007 collection rate—fourth straight year above 98% and second highest among North Carolina's largest urban counties behind Buncombe—while reducing prior-year uncollected taxes below $3 million and projecting a revenue-neutral 2008 revaluation rate in the high 60s or low 70s cents; Chair Reckhow also noted the ABC Board budgeted a $750,000 county payment. The Board approved the 2006 settlement and 2007 tax charge 4-0, announced ballot appointments (ABC Board, Durham Tech Trustees, EMS Advisory Council, Library Board, Nursing Home Advisory Board), and adjourned at 9:33 p.m.

votes.item_title: Excuse Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.
votes.notes: Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. absent/excused; 4-0 unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to excuse Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. from the July 23, 2007 regular session.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (Three Sets)
votes.notes: Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. excused; 4-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved three sets of minutes as submitted.

votes.item_title: Item 7H: $4.5M General Fund Balance Advance for Durham County Memorial Stadium Renovations
votes.notes: Split 3-1 voice vote with Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. excused. Among the four present commissioners, Becky M. Heron moved, Michael D. Page seconded, Ellen W. Reckhow presided and pulled the item on the County Attorney's guidance, and Lewis A. Cheek was the sole member casting the recorded Nay vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Budget ordinance and capital project amendment advancing $4,500,000 from General Fund balance for the Durham County Memorial Stadium renovation project, with a reimbursement resolution for spring 2008 financing under G.S. 160A-20. One commissioner asked to record his vote as No, stating he had previously expressed his opinion and did not believe it was a good expenditure of county funds.

votes.item_title: 2006 Property Tax Settlement Report, 2007 Tax Charge, and Relief of Delinquent Taxes
votes.notes: Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. excused; 4-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Received and approved the 2006 property tax settlement report, charged the Tax Collector with 2007 property taxes, and authorized relief of real/personal property taxes over 10 years past due and motor vehicle taxes over two years past due.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: $4.5 Million General Fund Balance Advance for Durham County Memorial Stadium Renovations (Item 7H)
disagreements.summary: During consideration of the July 23, 2007 consent agenda, Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek objected to advancing $4.5 million from General Fund balance for the Durham County Memorial Stadium renovation project and asked to be recorded as voting No, prompting the Board to pull Item 7H and approve it 3-1.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance $4.5 million from General Fund balance (to be reimbursed via spring 2008 financing) to move forward with Durham County Memorial Stadium renovations.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. excused out of town, the four seated commissioners unanimously approved performance-based salary adjustments for four department heads following a closed-session evaluation and adopted a resolution urging the General Assembly to pass the state budget by July 1, 2007 to clarify Medicaid relief and local mandates. The Board approved a broad consent agenda covering detention center maintenance and medical contracts, social services grants, a $7.62 million Lowe's Grove Middle School renovation contract, and a $500,000 mental health crisis center renovation at the Oakley Building, while pulling three items including a $927,109 federal farmland conservation grant for Little River Farm. Commissioners also received the proposed property revaluation schedule of values, introduced $207.1 million in November 2007 general obligation bond orders for Durham Public Schools, Durham Technical Community College, and the Museum of Life and Science, and appointed members to county advisory boards and Downtown Durham Inc.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge, and Excusal of Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow welcomed attendees to the June 25, 2007 regular meeting and led the Pledge of Allegiance. She noted that Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. was out of town and requested a motion to excuse him.

agenda_items.title: Department Head Performance Salary Increases
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a closed-session performance evaluation, the Board set new salaries reflecting performance for four county department heads: Tax Administrator Ken Joyner at $109,000, Sheriff Worth Hill at $116,000, Register of Deeds Willie Covington at $103,000, and County Attorney Chuck Kitchen at $160,000.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board added a Downtown Durham Inc. board appointment before Item 17 and added Consent Item 7U for an American Red Cross nonprofit grant amendment. Commissioners then approved the minutes from the June 4 work session and June 11 regular session.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Requesting State Budget Adoption by July 1, 2007
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Becky M. Heron read a resolution urging the Governor and North Carolina General Assembly to adopt the state budget by July 1, 2007 so counties can meet statutory balanced-budget deadlines. The resolution highlighted pending state mandates and uncertainty over whether Medicaid relief would be temporary, permanent, or enacted at all, and directed copies to all 100 counties and North Carolina legislators.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 7A-7U, excluding pulled 7I, 7N, 7S)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed a lengthy consent agenda including contracts for Detention Center maintenance ($414,266) and inmate medical care ($2,598,800), Animal Protection Society shelter operations ($571,997), May 2007 property tax releases, Lowe's Grove Middle School renovation ($7,620,000), Oakley Building mental health crisis center renovation ($500,000 Duke University funds), and a $5,000 Red Cross grant redistribution. Items 7I, 7N, and 7S were pulled for separate discussion.

agenda_items.title: Federal Farm and Ranch Lands Protection Grant Agreement (Little River Farm)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow pulled Item 7I so the County Manager could highlight Durham County's receipt of a $927,109 grant through the Commodity Credit Corporation for permanent farmland conservation easements at Little River Farm in Northern Durham. Officials noted it was the largest Farm and Ranch Lands Protection grant awarded in the state.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Revaluation Schedule of Values, Standards, and Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board received the proposed schedule of values, standards, and rules for property tax revaluation and scheduled a public hearing for July 23, 2007. Staff was directed to publish required notices of public inspection and hearing times in the Durham Herald-Sun.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of 2007 General Obligation Bond Orders ($207.1 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board introduced three bond orders totaling $207,100,000 ($194,240,000 for Durham Public Schools, $8,680,000 for Durham Technical Community College, and $4,180,000 for the Museum of Life and Science), received the Finance Director's sworn statement of debt, and set a public hearing for July 23, 2007 ahead of a November referendum. Speakers E. Lavonia Allison and Victoria Peterson criticized recent tax increases and questioned school siting equity and land acquisition transparency, while commissioners discussed whether remaining 2000 bond funds could address cafeteria or band room needs.

agenda_items.title: Appointment to Downtown Durham Inc. Board
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Commissioner Michael D. Page's completion of a two-year term, the Board appointed Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek to serve as the county representative on the Downtown Durham Inc. board. Commissioner Page briefly objected jokingly before withdrawing his objection.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed whether to hold off on Juvenile Crime Prevention Council appointments or waive maximum-term limits so experienced members could continue upcoming program monitoring. The Clerk subsequently announced ballot selections across 14 boards and commissions, and commissioners briefly clarified residency rules in the planning interlocal agreement for a Planning Commission appointee on Latta Road.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Business Location or Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss matters relating to the location or expansion of business or industry. Upon returning, the Chair reported that direction was given to staff, no action was taken, and the meeting adjourned at 9:25 PM.

votes.item_title: Excuse Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.
votes.notes: Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. excused/absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Reckhow noted Commissioner Cousin was out of town.

votes.item_title: Approve Department Head Salary Increases (Joyner, Hill, Covington, Kitchen)
votes.notes: Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Set annual salaries following closed-session evaluations: Ken Joyner $109,000, Worth Hill $116,000, Willie Covington $103,000, and Chuck Kitchen $160,000.

votes.item_title: Approve Minutes (June 4 Work Session and June 11 Regular Session)
votes.notes: Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved both sets of minutes without changes.

votes.item_title: Approve Consent Agenda (excluding Items 7I, 7N, and 7S)
votes.notes: Items 7I, 7N, and 7S pulled for separate consideration; Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved Detention Center maintenance and medical contracts, Animal Shelter lease/contract, tax releases, Lowe's Grove renovation ($7.62M), Oakley Building crisis center design/renovation, added Item 7U (Red Cross), and related fiscal items.

votes.item_title: Receive Revaluation Schedule of Values and Set July 23 Public Hearing
votes.notes: Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Received proposed schedule of value standards and rules, scheduled public hearing for July 23, and directed advertisement in the Durham Herald-Sun.

votes.item_title: Introduce 2007 Bond Orders ($207.1M), Receive Sworn Statement of Debt, and Set July 23 Public Hearing
votes.notes: Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Introduced $194.24M DPS, $8.68M Durham Tech, and $4.18M Museum of Life and Science bond orders and set July 23, 2007 public hearing toward a November referendum.

votes.item_title: Appoint Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek to Downtown Durham Inc. Board
votes.notes: Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Commissioner Cheek to replace Commissioner Page on the Downtown Durham Inc. board.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
votes.notes: Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to discuss business or industry location or expansion.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek returned from a six-week medical leave for alcoholism recovery, and all five seated commissioners participated in unanimous votes throughout the session. Following a public hearing on the $760.8 million FY 2007-2008 recommended budget—where County Manager Mike Ruffin highlighted Medicaid and education cost pressures and nonprofit leaders urged adoption of recommended grants—the Board approved consent items including $101,000 in Smart Start and adoption funds for Social Services after citizen comment on foster care. Commissioners also unanimously approved the 140-lot Ravenstone Phase III cluster subdivision with an 18% perimeter lot-size reduction and 20 acres of preserved open space, and adopted a preliminary resolution for November 2007 general obligation bond issues ($194.24 million for Durham Public Schools, $8.68 million for Durham Technical Community College, and museum bonds) after removing $3.3 million for future High School B land.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Welcome Back of Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek gave a personal statement announcing his return from a six-week medical leave in the North Carolina mountains to address burnout and an April relapse in his recovery from alcoholism, pledging renewed dedication to Durham's poor, homeless, addicted, and mentally ill residents. Chair Ellen W. Reckhow welcomed him back in time for budget finalization, and Vice Chair Becky M. Heron announced an Adopt-a-Cat Day at the animal shelter on June 23.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (including May 22 Budget Work Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow noted minor typographical corrections changing 'whole' to 'hold' in two places on pages two and three of the May 22, 2007 budget work session minutes. The Board unanimously approved all four sets of minutes as corrected.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation in Recognition of Juneteenth
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read a proclamation recognizing Juneteenth, tracing its origin to June 19, 1865 in Galveston, Texas and encouraging residents to support community celebrations and historical understanding.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A, 6C-6F, 6H-6I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 6G was removed from the agenda and Item 6B was pulled for a citizen speaker. The Board unanimously approved the remaining items, including $98,719 from Shaw University for Durham County Stadium improvements, Medicaid pass-through adjustments, a $3,000 PROUD program appropriation, NACo voting delegate designation for Chair Reckhow, an upset-bid surplus sale at 2415 State Street, a reimbursement resolution for the Justice Center and Human Services Building, and a Cultural Master Plan grant.

agenda_items.title: Department of Social Services Budget Ordinance Amendment ($101,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The item recognized $5,000 for the Smart Start childcare subsidy and $96,000 for the Special Children Adoption Fund. Citizen Victoria Peterson spoke regarding challenges African American families face navigating the foster care system, and the Board unanimously approved the amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2007-2008 Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Mike Ruffin presented highlights of the $760.8 million recommended budget ($642.9 million General Fund), noting that property and sales taxes account for 68% of revenue, human services (35.7 cents/dollar) and education (over 29 cents/dollar) lead spending, and county Medicaid costs total $13.7 million. Representatives from nonprofit agencies—including Alliance of AIDS Services Carolina, Urban Ministries of Durham ($185,000 grant), and Achievement Academy of Durham—spoke in support of recommended county funding, and the Board noted budget work sessions would continue ahead of June 25 adoption.

agenda_items.title: Major Site Plan and Preliminary Plan: Ravenstone Phase III
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning Director Frank Duke presented a 140-lot single-family cluster subdivision on approximately 59 acres south of Hillview Drive, west of Rondalay Drive, and east of Sharon Road, requesting discretionary approval of perimeter lots 18% smaller than the 10,000-square-foot base zoning. Commissioners praised the trail system around 20 acres of preserved open space and cooperation on Little Lick Creek stream restoration before approving unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Preliminary Resolution on 2007 General Obligation Bond Issues
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney presented the preliminary bond resolution initiating Local Government Commission application and appointing Robinson Bradshaw as bond counsel for a planned November 2007 referendum covering $194,240,000 for Durham Public Schools, $8,680,000 for Durham Technical Community College, and NC Museum of Life and Science bonds. Staff noted a $3.3 million reduction from the earlier draft for Durham Public Schools by deferring land acquisition for a future High School B to the planned 2009 bond referendum.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Legal Claim and Attorney-Client Privilege
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to adjourn to closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to discuss a claim and consult with the county attorney. After returning to open session, the Chair reported direction was given to staff, no action was taken, and the meeting adjourned at 8:35 PM.

votes.item_title: Approve Minutes (including Corrected May 22 Budget Work Session)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved four sets of minutes with minor typographical corrections to May 22 minutes.

votes.item_title: Approve Item 6B: DSS Budget Ordinance Amendment ($101,000)
votes.discussion_detail: Recognized $5,000 Smart Start childcare subsidy and $96,000 Special Children Adoption Fund revenue following public comment by Victoria Peterson.

votes.item_title: Approve Ravenstone Phase III Preliminary Plan and Major Site Plan
votes.discussion_detail: Approved 140-lot cluster subdivision with discretionary 18% reduction in perimeter lot sizes and trail/stream restoration features.

votes.item_title: Adopt Preliminary Resolution on 2007 General Obligation Bond Issues
votes.notes: Transcript ASR rendered museum bond amount as '$480,000' at 00:57:52; subsequent June 25 meeting states $4,180,000.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted preliminary resolution for school ($194,240,000), community college ($8,680,000), and museum bonds, removing $3.3M for future High School B land.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to discuss a claim and consult with the county attorney.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Operating with a three-member quorum while Commissioners Lewis A. Cheek and Michael D. Page were excused, the Board unanimously recognized Sheriff's Deputy Shane Fowler as Employee of the Year and honored outgoing North Carolina Central University Chancellor James H. Ammons. Commissioners approved consent agenda items including a $10.35 million Durham Center revenue reclassification, $60,000 in acoustical design services for the Human Services Complex, and surplus property sales, and adopted a Unified Development Ordinance text amendment permitting animated downtown signs while barring animated off-premise billboards. Following extensive discussion with neighboring residents and planning staff regarding stormwater runoff from Meadowvale and county versus city stream-buffer rules, the Board approved the Traver Commons site/zoning plan with an added fencing condition, made four board appointments, and authorized an $8,500-per-acre purchase offer for the Lee property along the Little River after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Excusal of Commissioners Michael D. Page and Lewis A. Cheek and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow noted Commissioners Michael D. Page and Lewis A. Cheek were excused, leaving a three-member quorum with Vice Chair Becky M. Heron and Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. The Board approved the excusal of Commissioner Page and adopted minutes including corrected May 14 attendance.

agenda_items.title: Employee of the Year Recognition: Sheriff's Deputy Shane Fowler
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board recognized Sheriff's Office Deputy Shane Fowler, a four-year veteran assigned to the bomb squad, as Employee of the Year following peer selection. Remarks highlighted his work ethic, diligence with stolen property investigations, and community service.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Appearance Commission report)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved consent items including April 2007 tax releases, a $10,350,000 Durham Center revenue reclassification, $13,366 in public library aid, a $60,000 Freelon Group acoustical design contract for the Human Services Complex, annual reports from the Design District Review Team and Environmental Affairs Board, Cultural Master Plan interlocal extension, surplus property sales, and the 2007-2009 Workforce Block Grant Plan revision. Commissioner Cousin later asked the Manager for a follow-up briefing on workforce plan execution.

agenda_items.title: City-County Appearance Commission Annual Report (Pulled Consent Item)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Heron pulled the Appearance Commission annual report to commend the Golden Leaf Awards ceremony, Hildegard Ryals's recognition, and Chair Reckhow noted the Museum of Life and Science BioQuest project award. The Board then approved the item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Recognizing NCCU Chancellor James H. Ammons
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Moved later in the agenda for Chancellor James H. Ammons's arrival, the Board read a formal resolution honoring his six years at North Carolina Central University, noting enrollment growth of 58.4% to 8,675 students, over $40 million in private fundraising, and establishment of the Josephine Dobbs Clement Early College High School.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment on Animated or Motion Signs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Frank Duke presented a Unified Development Ordinance text amendment allowing animated signs downtown while clarifying that off-premise billboards may not use animated sign faces. Noting unanimous Planning Commission (11-0) and City Council approval, the Board adopted the amendment unanimously without public opposition.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change / Site Plan (Traver Commons)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: First Carolina Properties requested a zoning map change for Traver Commons, prompting neighboring residents from The Oaks to request a delay, buffering/fencing along existing homes, and relief from stormwater runoff originating in the city-approved Meadowvale development. Planning Director Frank Duke explained that deferring until city annexation would eliminate county stream-buffer protections on small drainage basins, and the Board approved the project 3-0 with an added fencing condition while asking staff to meet with city stormwater officials.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With only one application received for the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee, the Board agreed to re-advertise that vacancy. The Clerk announced appointments of Bill Ruffin (Civic Center Authority), Allen D. Goldstein (Criminal Justice Partnership Advisory Board), Rene L. Johnson (Industrial Facilities and Pollution Control Authority), and William Grueling (Open Space and Trails Commission).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Post-Session Offer to Purchase Little River Property
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board entered closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding potential acquisition of properties owned by James and Robert E. Lee (0 Johnson Mill Rd) and Alton B. Smith Jr. (8211 Johnson Mill Rd). Upon returning to open session, commissioners unanimously authorized an $8,500-per-acre offer to purchase the Lee property on the Little River (ID 190123), closing by January 31, 2008, contingent on 50% grant assistance and a satisfactory Phase I environmental site assessment.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Special Session
meetings.executive_summary: At a special session convened solely for presentation of the FY 2007-2008 recommended budget—with Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek excused—County Manager Mike Ruffin delivered a $760.8 million spending plan across 21 funds, including a $642.9 million General Fund. Ruffin reviewed Durham County's Results-Based Accountability framework, state and national financial and human-services awards, and individual employee impact stories before detailing budget priorities such as pay-plan maintenance, a 10% health insurance increase, $210,924 for substance abuse outpatient treatment, and top-tier per-pupil school funding. He warned that escalating Medicaid and public school costs cannot be sustained solely through property taxes—estimating a $58.20 annual impact on a $150,000 home—and outlined June public hearing and work session dates leading to final adoption on June 25. No votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Excusal of Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the special budget presentation meeting and announced that Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek was excused. She turned the floor over to County Manager Mike Ruffin to present the FY 2007-2008 recommended budget.

agenda_items.title: County Manager's FY 2007-2008 Recommended Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Mike Ruffin presented the $760.8 million recommended budget ($642.9 million General Fund), highlighting GFOA reporting awards, NCACC awards for Rapid Response Homes and DSS initiatives, employee stories including Lt. C.R. Bone and social worker Robert Wallace, and Results-Based Accountability progress. Key fiscal items included pay-plan maintenance, a 10% ($452,880) health insurance increase, $210,924 for a Durham Center outpatient substance abuse program, $166,623 for adult and child systems of care, a projected General Fund balance increase to 14.15%, and a property tax impact of $58.20 per year on a $150,000 home, alongside a request from the RTP Service District advisory committee to double its rate from 1.87 to 3.74 cents.

agenda_items.title: Board Remarks and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow thanked the County Manager and underscored the need for General Assembly action to relieve counties of Medicaid and school funding pressures on property taxpayers, while another commissioner praised the employee recognition stories. The special meeting adjourned at 5:43 PM ahead of the 7:00 PM Durham County Stadium community meeting at Northern High School.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek excused, the four seated commissioners unanimously approved all actions taken during the session, beginning with Foster Care Month and Soil and Water Conservation team recognitions and announcements on upcoming Durham County Stadium and budget meetings. The Board adopted most of the consent agenda—including an offer to purchase 50 acres on the Little River for $550,000 contingent on state grant funding, Oakley Building and Stadium RFQ exemptions, and $150,000 for revaluation assistance—and separately approved FY 2007-2008 JCPC allocations (excluding one item), a $140,000 Scott King Road stormwater escrow transfer to Durham Public Schools, and a school construction contract. Following a public hearing, commissioners also unanimously approved up to $1 million in economic development incentives for Computer Sciences Corporation's Research Triangle Park expansion before adjourning into closed session on an alleged criminal misconduct investigation.

Cheek was excused, added a closed session, announced a May 21 community meeting on Durham County Stadium improvements at Northern High School, and outlined a condensed May/June budget work session schedule; Vice Chair Heron promoted the May 19 Walk for the Animals. The Board then approved the April 23 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Foster Care Month Proclamation and Soil & Water Team Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read the Foster Care Month proclamation noting 266 Durham County children in foster care and invited DSS Child Placement Manager Javetta Whitfield and Deputy Sheriff Lisa Richmond to speak. agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (excluding pulled 7F, 7G, 7H and deferred 7O)

agenda_items.title: FY 2007-2008 JCPC / DJJDP Program Funding Allocations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Vice Chair Heron for discussion, the Board reviewed the recommended Juvenile Crime Prevention Council / Department of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention program allocations for FY 2007-2008. agenda_items.title: Scott King Road Stormwater Escrow Transfer to Durham Public Schools ($140,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow pulled Item 7G to add a condition transferring $140,000 from the Scott King Road stormwater infrastructure escrow account to Durham Public Schools designated for capital improvements, paid directly by the state. agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Construction Contract (Pulled by Citizen)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by a citizen raising questions about African American subcontractor participation, Chair Reckhow explained that the county administers DPS construction contracts solely to capture state sales tax exemptions for the school system rather than actively tracking subcontractor demographics. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Commissioners excused Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek through the end of May for medical leave and celebrated National County Government Week alongside recognitions for volunteers, DSS's Latino Ombudsman Program award, Older Americans Month, and Mental Health Awareness Month. The four seated commissioners unanimously approved the consent agenda—including a $16.6 million Durham Center Medicaid budget adjustment and the FY 2007-2008 HUD Annual Action Plan—along with removing a parcel from the Research Triangle Park Service District and rezoning 1423-1427 Bungalow Avenue to RS-10. agenda_items.title: Excusal of Commissioner Cheek, Gang Study Update, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to excuse Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek through the end of May due to medical issues. Chair Reckhow reported that Deputy County Manager Wendell Davis was arranging a meeting among school board, city, and county leadership on the gang study, and commissioners announced the May 5 Durham Reads Together event and May 19 Walk for the Animals.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed and approved three sets of prior meeting minutes without changes.

agenda_items.title: National County Government Week, DSS Award, and Monthly Proclamations

Commissioners also recognized DSS for its NCACC Outstanding Program Award for the Latino Ombudsman Program, reviewed 2006 child welfare figures (2,307 assessments, 474 substantiated cases, 117 custody assumptions), and read proclamations for Older Americans Month and Mental Health Awareness Month.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 11A-11O)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved consent items including March 2007 tax releases, Cultural Master Plan grants ($29,900 and $20,000), closing the Reappraisal Reserve Fund ($269,850.15 transfer to General Fund), a $16.6 million Durham Center budget decrease reflecting changed Medicaid payment flows, a 13-month $380,900 HealthStat wellness clinic contract, and the FY 2007-2008 HUD Annual Action Plan (CDBG, HOME, ADDI, ESG).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following remarks by attorney Patrick Byker and confirmation of Research Triangle Park Foundation support for property north of Hopson Road, the Board held a public hearing and unanimously adopted the resolution removing the territory from the RTP Service District.

disagreements.issue: Cost and Fiscal Timing of DSS Lease Agreement with Genesis Home
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-1 over approving a $45,000-per-year (plus utilities) DSS lease for 4,400 square feet at Genesis Home, weighing family support needs against taxpayer sensitivity before the November bond referendum.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the DSS lease with Genesis Home to support family reunification and frontline social workers.
side_a_arguments: Provides a warm, comfortable family environment to help dysfunctional or disadvantaged families re-enter mainstream society.
Supports social workers handling gang violence, poverty, and school-related family challenges who are frequently asked to work across Durham without extra compensation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the lease as an expensive expenditure given taxpayer frustration and upcoming bond votes.
side_b_arguments: Paying $45,000 per year plus utilities and phone/computer lines for 4,400 square feet represents a high-dollar facility commitment.
Taxpayers are already strained and approaching a November bond referendum, risking perceptions of excessive county spending.
disagreements.resolution: Motion carried 3-1 with Vice Chair Becky M. Heron dissenting.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. excused due to illness, the four seated commissioners celebrated Vice Chair Becky M. Heron's Jaycees Outstanding Senior Citizen Award and proclaimed April 17 as National Library Workers' Day after a performance by the Library Precision Book Cart Drill Team. The Board unanimously approved a consent agenda including $80,000 returned to the Redwood Volunteer Fire Department, over $4.2 million in school capital amendments for Fayetteville Street and New B elementary schools, and a $355,536 sole-source GangNet software contract for the Sheriff's Office. On an ordinance prohibiting roadway solicitation in the unincorporated county, the Board split 3-1: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, Vice Chair Becky M. Heron, and Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek voted Aye to enhance traffic safety and link panhandlers to social-service resources, while Commissioner Michael D. Page voted Nay because the city had not adopted a parallel ban and he feared punitive law enforcement against homeless individuals; because it received only three affirmative votes, a second reading was scheduled for April 23.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Adjustments, Excusal of Commissioner Cousin, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board deleted Item 9, added Item 10A to consider moving a June budget work session, and unanimously excused Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. due to illness. Chair Reckhow also congratulated Vice Chair Becky M. Heron on receiving the 2007 Durham Jaycees Outstanding Senior Citizen Award and noted April as Child Abuse Prevention Month.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed and unanimously approved several sets of prior meeting minutes without changes.

agenda_items.title: Library Precision Book Cart Drill Team and National Library Workers' Day Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Durham County Library Precision Book Cart Drill Team performed before Chair Reckhow proclaimed April 17, 2007 as National Library Workers' Day. Library Director Skip Auld highlighted the Durham Reads Together selection 'The Last Shot' and upcoming author visit on May 5.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 6A-6I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved nine consent items, including returning $80,000 in unspent salary funds to Redwood Volunteer Fire Department, approving a Fayetteville Street Elementary construction contract and capital amendments ($2,390,392 for Fayetteville St and $1,822,305 for New B Elementary), designating SRA as sole-source provider for Sheriff's Office GangNet software ($355,536), accepting the Development Review Board and Planning Commission 2006 annual reports, amending the DACA lease at 1201 Briggs Ave, donating surplus property to Durham Tech, appropriating $200,000 for risk management, and approving The Durham Center's 2007-2010 business plan. Afterward, Vice Chair Heron raised concerns about late Thursday packet delivery for Friday DRB meetings and asked staff for follow-up on Planning Commission recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Roadway Solicitation Ban Ordinance (First Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek moved approval of an ordinance banning roadway solicitation outside city limits paired with a social-service resource sheet for individuals on roadways, supported by Chair Reckhow and Vice Chair Heron as a pedestrian safety and outreach measure on high-speed arterials. Commissioner Michael D. Page opposed the county-only ban as premature without city participation and warned it could subject homeless residents to unwelcoming law enforcement. The motion carried 3-1, requiring a second reading on April 23 due to Commissioner Cousin's absence.

agenda_items.title: June Budget Work Session Schedule Adjustment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to Commissioner Page's scheduling conflict on June 14, the Board agreed to cancel the June 14 budget work session and hold a working lunch session from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM on Monday, June 11 prior to that evening's budget public hearing.

Returning at 9:27 PM, the Board reported direction was given to staff with no action taken.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-1 on enacting a ban on roadway solicitation in unincorporated Durham County paired with a resource list for deputies, debating pedestrian safety and outreach versus potential punitive enforcement against homeless individuals without a parallel city ordinance.
disagreements.side_a_position: Enact the county roadway solicitation ban paired with a social-service resource sheet for deputies.
side_a_arguments: Soliciting on county arterials with 45-55 mph traffic is physically unsafe for individuals in or beside the roadway.
The ordinance is not intended to jail people, but to serve as a compassionate vehicle for deputies to distribute a condensed resource list connecting people to mental health and shelter services.
County action could encourage the City of Durham to adopt a similar ordinance.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose enacting the county ban at this time without a joint city-county framework and stronger homeless services.
side_b_arguments: Most roadway solicitation occurs inside city limits, yet the City of Durham has not enacted a corresponding ordinance.
Homeless residents on the streets are in dire need of help and services, and passing a ban signals law enforcement to enforce it in a way that feels unwelcoming to the community.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 3-1 on first reading with Michael D. Page voting Nay; because fewer than four affirmative votes were cast, the ordinance was scheduled for a second reading on April 23.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: The Board opened with proclamations including Durham Take a Stand Alcohol Awareness Day with speaker Wanda Boone and unanimously approved a consent agenda covering February 2007 property tax releases, public health grants, library board bylaw revisions, surplus property sales, a $60,000 NextGen digital document amendment, and a $57,000 Judicial Building second-floor renovation design contract. Commissioners held a public hearing on a county-initiated Page Road Suburban Transit Area comprehensive plan amendment—where a resident opposed industrial re-designation and Crosland's attorney supported office/research uses while opposing heavy industry—and later unanimously approved a 276-lot residential development plan featuring a span stream crossing limiting flood-fringe fill to roughly 2.5% while preserving prior lot-size commitments. agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Durham Take a Stand Alcohol Awareness Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow recognized Norma Martin on a board proclamation signed by all five commissioners and read the Durham Take a Stand Alcohol Awareness Day proclamation detailing the health, safety, and youth-risk impacts of alcohol misuse. Wanda Boone offered remarks following the proclamation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 11A-11G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved seven consent items, including February 2007 tax releases, Public Health grants ($1,000 for Partnership for a Healthy Durham and $14,000 for syphilis elimination), Library Board of Trustees bylaw revisions, surplus property sales to Briscoe Enterprises (312 East End Ave for $4,200, 811 Chalmers St for $3,500, and 2715 Marlon Dr for $2,000), a $60,000 NextGen Digital Document Solutions amendment, and a $57,000 DTW Architects design contract for the second floor of the Judicial Building.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Plan Amendment for Page Road Suburban Transit Area
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Frank Duke presented a county-initiated comprehensive plan amendment to re-designate parcels on the west side of Page Road south of Globe Road to industrial, noting a 12-0 Planning Commission recommendation. Resident Cameron Sharon opposed the industrial change, Crosland attorney Patrick Byker (adjacent 400-acre mixed-use 'Bess Page' project) urged light office/research rather than heavy industrial or warehousing, and 32-acre landowner James Connell spoke; Commissioner Cheek noted a plan amendment does not rezone property.

agenda_items.title: Site Plan / Development Plan with Span Crossing and Floodplain Fill

Vice Chair Heron raised concerns about late DRB packet delivery, new floodplain maps, and runoff, while staff confirmed prior lot-size proffers (committed elements #4 and #18) remained intact; the Board approved the plan unanimously after the attorney clarified voting rules.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: All five commissioners participated in unanimous votes on the minutes, consent agenda, economic development incentives, and closed session. After correcting the February 26 minutes regarding Gary Wallace's support and clarifying Vice Chair Becky M. Heron's recusal procedure, the Board presented Professional Social Work Month recognition, honored Erosion Control staffer Joe Pierce with the Anchor Award, and heard an RDU Airport briefing on ExpressJet service expansion and Terminal C Phase 2 construction. Commissioners unanimously approved a consent agenda featuring the CodeRED 911 alert interlocal agreement, a letter supporting state regulation of handgun ammunition sales, $324,900 for surplus sales at 300-306 East Main Street (earmarked toward the capital plan), Judicial Building elevator upgrades, and a $223,900 South Regional Library design amendment. Following a public hearing marked by procedural friction when speaker Victoria Peterson sought to cross-examine company representatives, the Board unanimously approved up to $100,000 in relocation and training incentives for Nitronex Corporation.

agenda_items.title: EITC/VITA Outreach Announcement and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A commissioner highlighted Earned Income Tax Credit and VITA free tax-filing efforts aimed at capturing an estimated $2 million to $5 million in unclaimed local credits and supporting state EITC legislation. Commissioners then approved two sets of minutes after correcting the February 26 record to reflect that Gary Wallace favored the plan and clarifying that Vice Chair Heron could vote on her own recusal motion even when recused from the underlying zoning item.

agenda_items.title: Professional Social Work Month Proclamation and March Anchor Award (Joe Pierce)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow proclaimed March 2007 as Professional Social Work Month and welcomed DSS Director Sammy Haithcock. Staff then presented the March Anchor Award to Erosion Control officer Joe Pierce, reading commendations from southern Durham County citizens praising his responsiveness and professionalism.

agenda_items.title: Raleigh-Durham International Airport (RDU) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Airport officials briefed the Board on ExpressJet launching 13 daily departures to six cities, West Coast and potential Frankfurt service demand, new terminal concessions, and Terminal C Phase 2 construction targeted for late 2010 completion. Commissioners suggested creating a cell-phone waiting lot to ease curbside pickup congestion and urged parity for Terminal A.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 7A-7I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved all nine consent items, including the Criminal Justice Partnership Program grant application, $123,167 in bond issuance costs, the CodeRED emergency notification interlocal agreement with the City of Durham, a legislative delegation letter supporting handgun ammunition sales regulation, Judicial Building elevator modernization (within $360,030 budget), a $223,900 Freelon Group design amendment for South Regional Branch Library, and surplus sales at 300/306 East Main Street ($324,900), 2304 Hart Street ($7,400), and 1206 Linwood Avenue ($1,380). Chair Reckhow asked the Manager to transfer the $324,900 East Main Street proceeds into the Capital Finance Plan in the upcoming budget to offset tax-rate pressure.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentives for Nitronex Corporation ($100,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chamber CEO Libby Barnes and Deputy County Manager Carolyn Titus presented Nitronex Corporation's planned relocation from Raleigh to Durham County, involving $24 million in investment, 200 net new jobs over five years, and up to $100,000 in relocation and training reimbursements. When speaker Victoria Peterson attempted to quiz company officials directly, Commissioner Cheek objected that cross-examining businesses during a public hearing was out of order, while Commissioner Page suggested staff include company workforce histories in future packets; the Board approved the incentives unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Business Location or Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to adjourn to closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business or industry location or expansion. Returning at 9:22 PM, the Board reported direction was given to staff with no action taken.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: With all five commissioners seated, the Board welcomed Boy Scout Troop 486, approved prior minutes with follow-up requested on joint school board action items, and unanimously passed a consent agenda renewing the five-year city-county property tax collection agreement and approving $821,507.87 in COPS-funded Sheriff's radio equipment and $303,884 in wastewater collection rehabilitation. meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 12, 2007 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously (4-0) excused Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek, approved three sets of minutes with one supervision correction, and adopted the consent agenda excluding pulled items 8A, 8D, 8J, 8K, and 8M after recognizing February Anchor Award winner Alina Spades and National Schools to Watch winners Carrington and Shepard Middle Schools. Following a 10-minute recess and County Attorney advice warning that approving a development plan with a staff-cited technical ordinance violation on a four-member board risked litigation, a contested rezoning/development application zoned R-20 failed on a 2-2 voice vote (Ayes: Becky M. Heron, Ellen W. Reckhow; Nays: Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr., Michael D. Page; Lewis A. Cheek excused). Commissioners later heard public opposition from Victoria Peterson to a proposed real estate transfer tax before voting 4-0 to move forward with the transfer tax proposal to fund school capital needs and reduce pressure on property taxes. The Board also met in closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), (4), and (6) regarding employee performance, business expansion, and County of Durham v. AREC 3 LLC, giving direction to staff before adjourning at 11:15 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek, Deferrals, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the meeting, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and requested a motion to excuse Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek, which passed unanimously (4-0). Reckhow announced that items 11 and 12 were deferred due to public hearing notification issues and asked the County Manager to establish notification checks and balances with the Planning Director, while Vice Chair Becky M. Heron announced a February 17 Animal Shelter open house.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (Three Sets, Including December 11 Correction)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow identified a correction on page 17 of the December 11 minutes changing 'indirect' to 'direct supervision' after checking with the County Manager. Commissioners approved all three sets of minutes as corrected.

agenda_items.title: February Anchor Award Presentation: Alina Spades
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Elections Director Mike Ashe presented the February Anchor Award to Alina Spades for outstanding customer service and professionalism in support of the democratic process. Commissioners offered congratulatory remarks.

agenda_items.title: Resolutions Recognizing National Schools to Watch: Carrington and Shepard Middle Schools
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow read formal resolutions honoring Carrington Middle School and Shepard IB Middle School for being named National Schools to Watch—making Durham Public Schools the only district in North Carolina with more than two honorees. School leaders including Assistant Principal Erica Boone accepted the resolutions and noted Shepard's academic and city-championship athletic achievements.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed consent items spanning library design amendments ($66,871 with The Freelon Group, pulled as 8A), McDougall Terrace library hours, Cultural Master Plan grants (8D pulled), surplus property sales, a $175 Zostavax vaccine fee, grant and budget amendments for public health lead prevention ($15,000), CJRC (8J pulled), school impact fee interest ($2,739,432 total outlay, 8K pulled), Register of Deeds automation ($181,000), enterprise debt consolidation (8M pulled), a local farm processing study ($2,500), JCPC appointments, and SAP financial consulting ($65,000). Commissioners approved the consent agenda excluding pulled items 8A, 8D, 8J, 8K, and 8M.

agenda_items.title: Disputed R-20 Rezoning / Development Application Following Nine-Month Mediation Period
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a nine-month delay after an April 2006 Planning Commission report, commissioners debated a proposed R-20 development adjacent to game lands whose committed elements planning staff flagged as technically non-compliant with the zoning ordinance. The County Attorney cautioned that approving a technically non-compliant rezoning on a four-member board risked a successful legal challenge and noted a 2-2 tie would fail, while delaying would allow a five-member vote and technical correction; after a 10-minute recess, a motion to approve failed on a 2-2 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Real Estate Transfer Tax for School Capital Needs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson urged commissioners and legislators to oppose a real estate transfer tax, arguing it would burden first-time homebuyers and homeowners. Chair Ellen W. Reckhow explained that transfer tax revenues—projected to support roughly $335 million in debt service over 20 years—would help address $900 million in capital requests including Durham Public Schools' $176 million-plus bond request without solely relying on property tax increases, and distinguished it from a prepared food tax before the Board voted 4-0 to move forward.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), (4), and (6) to evaluate a public officer/employee, discuss business relocation or expansion, and consult counsel on County of Durham v. AREC 3 LLC. Upon reconvening at 04:07:19, Chair Reckhow reported that direction was given to staff with no action taken, and adjourned at 11:15 p.m.

votes.item_title: Excuse Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek from Meeting
votes.notes: Lewis A. Cheek was excused/absent for the entire meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow requested a motion to excuse absent Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek at the start of the regular session.

votes.item_title: Approve Three Sets of Minutes with December 11 Correction
votes.notes: Lewis A. Cheek excused; unanimous 4-0 voice vote among seated members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Minutes approved together with Chair Reckhow's correction on page 17 of the December 11 minutes changing 'indirect' to 'direct supervision'.

votes.item_title: Approve Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 8A, 8D, 8J, 8K, and 8M)
votes.notes: Lewis A. Cheek excused; middle portion of digest truncated after speaker Victoria Peterson began remarks on pulled items.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved all unpulled consent agenda items including library service plans, surplus property sales, vaccine fee establishment, health/public works budget amendments, JCPC appointments, and SAP consulting increase; items 8A, 8D, 8J, 8K, and 8M were pulled for separate discussion.

votes.item_title: Approve R-20 Rezoning / Development Application
votes.notes: Voice vote with four members present (Lewis A. Cheek excused); mover Becky M. Heron and seconder Ellen W. Reckhow constituted the two Ayes and the remaining present members (Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. and Michael D. Page) the two Nays.
votes.discussion_detail: After a 10-minute recess and legal counsel warning that a technical zoning ordinance violation created litigation exposure and that a 2-2 tie on a four-member board would fail, Vice Chair Becky M. Heron moved to approve and Chair Ellen W. Reckhow seconded; the motion failed on a 2-2 tie.

votes.item_title: Move Forward with Proposed Real Estate Transfer Tax for School Capital Needs (Item 12A)
votes.notes: Voice vote with no opposition ('Opposed? No. Motion carries.'); Lewis A. Cheek excused.
votes.discussion_detail: Board voted to advance the proposed real estate transfer tax option for school capital funding following public opposition from Victoria Peterson and discussion of $900 million in county capital requests.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session
votes.notes: Lewis A. Cheek excused; board reconvened at 04:07:19 with direction given to staff and no action taken.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), (4), and (6) regarding employee performance, business relocation/expansion, and County of Durham v. AREC 3 LLC.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: R-20 Rezoning / Development Application with Technical Ordinance Violation and Neighborhood Mediation Impasse
disagreements.summary: Commissioners deadlocked 2-2 over whether to vote to approve a disputed R-20 development application adjacent to game lands after a nine-month delay, amid planning staff findings of a technical ordinance violation and County Attorney warnings of litigation risk.
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring the R-20 application to a vote for approval on the floor.
side_a_arguments: Moved and seconded to place the approval motion before the Board following a 10-minute recess rather than leaving the matter unresolved indefinitely.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose approving the application as submitted.
side_b_arguments: The applicant returned after nine months without resolving neighborhood concerns or changing the plan.
Planning staff was not directly involved in neighborhood negotiations and identified a technical violation of the zoning ordinance.
The R-20 land adjacent to game lands should be redesigned with a more environmentally sensitive plan rather than approved in non-compliant form.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to approve failed on a 2-2 tie with Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek excused.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 22, 2007 regular session, Chair Ellen W. Reckhow delivered the first annual State of Durham County address, highlighting Durham's AAA bond ratings, 80.9-cent tax rate, 98.5% tax collection rate, 2,902 new jobs led by biotech growth, protection of over 1,000 acres of open space, and $931 million in 10-year capital needs including Durham Public Schools facilities. With Commissioner Michael D. Page previously excused, the three remaining commissioners unanimously (3-0) excused absent Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek, held a public hearing on FY 2007–2008 HUD Consolidated Plan housing priorities, and approved (3-0) two Unified Development Ordinance text changes covering swimming pool yard fencing and 16 technical/wireless revisions. The Board also unanimously (3-0) appointed Page to the Carolina Theatre Board and Vice Chair Becky M. Heron to a county board, before entering closed session (3-0) and returning to approve a settlement proposal (3-0) for the Mansour property in County v. Mansour (06 CVS 6649) with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: First Annual State of Durham County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow delivered the county's inaugural State of Durham County address, noting AAA bond ratings from S&P and Moody's, a flat 80.9-cent property tax rate, a record 98.5% tax collection rate, and 2,902 announced jobs in 2006 led by Quintiles' 1,000-job expansion. She also highlighted protecting over 1,000 acres of open space, opening W.G. Pearson Elementary and the Hillside High band suite, Results-Based Accountability progress, and upcoming challenges in graduation rates, workforce training, and $931 million in 10-year capital requests.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow called the regular business session to order, noted Commissioner Michael D. Page was previously excused, and led a 3-0 vote excusing Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek due to sudden travel. She added the appointment of Page to the Carolina Theatre Board prior to closed session, and Vice Chair Becky M. Heron began announcing an Animal Protection Society shelter open house.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2007–2008 Consolidated Plan and HUD Federal Funds Needs Assessment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined four Consolidated Plan priority areas—neighborhood stabilization and revitalization, special needs housing, homeownership, and housing rehabilitation and repair—to guide FY 2007–2008 HUD grant applications. Public speakers Victoria Peterson, Rich Lee, and Laurie Sisabel commented, and Chair Reckhow asked staff to address Peterson's remarks linking neighborhood stabilization to crime reduction and reduced jail pressure.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change — Swimming Pool Fencing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning Director Frank Duke presented a UDO text amendment codifying his interpretation that a swimming pool inside a yard already enclosed by a fence does not require a second perimeter fence around the pool, alongside technical terminology alignments. Following a 7-3 Planning Commission recommendation and unanimous City Council adoption, the Board held a public hearing with no speakers and approved the amendment 3-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change — Technical Changes #2
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Frank Duke reviewed 16 technical UDO revisions addressing terminology inconsistencies and reorganizing wireless communication facility provisions to conform to the UDO's structure, which had received unanimous Planning Commission approval on October 10. With no speakers signed up, the Board closed the public hearing and approved the revisions 3-0.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments: Carolina Theatre Board and County Board Assignment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow noted Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek asked to leave the Carolina Theatre Board due to meeting time conflicts and the Board voted 3-0 to appoint Commissioner Michael D. Page in his place. Following brief discussion with staff member Jane, Vice Chair Becky M. Heron agreed to accept an open county board seat (transcribed as 'arm lien board') and was appointed 3-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Approval of Mansour Property Settlement (06 CVS 6649)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board voted 3-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), (4), and (5) for attorney-client consultations on County v. Mansour (06 CVS 6649), DOT v. County (04 CVS 6391), and In re MK02J87, business location matters, and property acquisition negotiations on Matthews Road, Johnson Mill Road, and Becky Drive. Returning to open session at 04:03:16, the Board voted 3-0 to approve the Mansour property settlement related to the Human Services Complex and adjourned at 11:06 p.m.

votes.notes: Michael D. Page and Lewis A. Cheek excused/absent; 3-0 voice vote of members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Reckhow noted Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek had sudden travel and requested excusal, while Commissioner Michael D. Page had been excused at the January 8 meeting.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted UDO text change clarifying that pools inside an already-fenced yard do not require a second interior pool fence and aligning ordinance terminology.

votes.item_title: Adopt UDO Text Change: Technical Changes #2 (Item 13)
votes.notes: Michael D. Page and Lewis A. Cheek excused; unanimous 3-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted 16 technical UDO revisions resolving terminology inconsistencies and reorganizing wireless communication facility provisions.

votes.item_title: Appoint Commissioner Michael D. Page to Carolina Theatre Board
votes.notes: Michael D. Page and Lewis A. Cheek excused; unanimous 3-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Commissioner Michael D. Page to replace Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek on the Carolina Theatre Board due to Cheek's scheduling conflicts.

votes.item_title: Appoint Commissioner Becky M. Heron to County Board
votes.notes: Michael D. Page and Lewis A. Cheek excused; unanimous 3-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Vice Chair Becky M. Heron to fill a vacant county board seat (transcribed in ASR as 'arm lien board', coordinated with staff member Jane).

votes.notes: Michael D. Page and Lewis A. Cheek excused; unanimous 3-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), (4), and (5) for County v. Mansour, DOT v. County, In re MK02J87, business location matters, and real property acquisition negotiations.

votes.notes: Michael D. Page and Lewis A. Cheek excused; unanimous 3-0 voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Following closed session, the Board approved the settlement proposal discussed for the Mansour property related to the Human Services Complex (06 CVS 6649).
