meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 8, 2007 regular session, the Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved the December 4, 2006 work session minutes, honored off-duty EMS lifesaver Ray Poole with the December Anchor Award, and unveiled Durham County's new Granicus meeting webcasting platform. Commissioners unanimously adopted a Board of Health resolution urging the General Assembly to allow local food and lodging inspection fees to offset over $700,000 in annual mandated inspection costs, and unanimously approved a site expansion public hearing item, two technical Comprehensive Plan amendments (Jovin Northeast Creek and SECU East Durham), and a UDO text change repealing suburban and urban chain-link fencing rules. The Board also unanimously approved $83,168 in Open Space and Trails matching grants across four recipients, excused Commissioner Michael D. Page from the upcoming January 22 meeting, and entered closed session to discuss NCDOT v. County of Durham with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of December 4, 2006 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the meeting, announced spring applications for Durham Neighborhood College (due January 31) and a January 30 NCDOT East End Connector public meeting at Living Waters Church. The Board unanimously approved the minutes of the December 4, 2006 work session.

agenda_items.title: December Anchor Award Presentation: Ray Poole
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Medical Services Director Mike Smith presented the December Anchor Award to Ray Poole in recognition of helping save a person's life while working off duty. Chair Reckhow presented the honorary and monetary award checks on behalf of the Board.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of Granicus Webcasting System for Durham County Meetings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant County Manager Deborah Craig-Ray demonstrated Durham County's new Granicus webcasting system, enabling residents without cable access and county staff to stream meetings online and jump directly to specific agenda items. She noted plans to attach agenda backup materials and potentially expand video indexing to City-County Committee, Library Board, and Planning Board meetings.

agenda_items.title: Board of Health Resolution Seeking Local Food and Lodging Inspection Fee Authority
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Health Director Brian Letourneau and Environmental Health Director Robert Brown reported that mandated inspections of 591 restaurants, 174 food stands, 52 meat markets, and 63 lodging establishments cost Durham County over $700,000 annually while receiving under $13,000 from the state. The Board unanimously adopted the Board of Health resolution urging the General Assembly to authorize local inspection fees, and later clarified for a public speaker that the proposed fees were unrelated to a prepared food tax.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Item 8A Public Health HUD Grant Opening)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow introduced Consent Agenda item 8A, a Public Health budget ordinance amendment recognizing $59,206 in U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development grant revenue via NC DENR. Subsequent consent agenda items were omitted in the digest middle truncation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Expansion of Existing Approved Site and Roadway Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a presentation on a small expansion of an existing approved site with turn-lane roadway improvements and stream buffers, the Board opened the public hearing with three citizens signed up (Lee Lambert, Ron Horbeth, and Drew Marsh) and heard remarks from Lee Lambert of 522 Oak Crest Drive. After closing the public hearing, commissioners unanimously approved the item.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Plan Amendment — Jovin, Northeast Creek
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a technical Comprehensive Plan designation correction for the Jovin Northeast Creek property to align the plan with a more intense rezoning approved by the Board the previous June. With Planning Commission and staff recommending approval and no public speakers, the Board approved the amendment unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Plan Amendment — SECU East Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff explained a technical Comprehensive Plan correction for roughly nine acres previously rezoned by the Board years earlier, triggered by a State Employees' Credit Union proposal to build a bank branch. Following a 12-2 Planning Commission recommendation and no public speakers, the Board approved the amendment unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Change — Repeal of Chain Link Fencing Standards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff recommended repealing UDO restrictions on chain-link fencing in suburban and urban tiers because non-compliant fencing contractors were leaving property owners cited while undercutting compliant firms. Following concurrence from the Joint City-County Planning Committee, a 13-1 Planning Commission recommendation, and City Council repeal, the Board unanimously adopted the repeal after no public speakers came forward.

agenda_items.title: Open Space and Trails Commission Matching Grants Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Analyst Kevin Etheridge presented matching grant recommendations totaling $83,168 from an $85,000 budget across four projects out of 11 applications requesting $239,918: Ellerbe Creek Watershed Association ($4,710), Eno River Association, Watts Montessori PTA ($25,662), and Eno Valley Elementary PTA ($9,233). Commissioners asked whether other schools had applied and unanimously approved the funding recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Excusal of Commissioner Michael D. Page for January 22 and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Michael D. Page apologized for arriving late to the meeting and requested to be excused from the January 22, 2007 meeting due to a conference, which the Board approved unanimously. Commissioners then voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation regarding NCDOT v. County of Durham (04 CVS 6391).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (excuse Page); Passed unanimously (closed session)

votes.item_title: Approve Minutes of December 4, 2006 Work Session (Item 4)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Commissioner Michael D. Page later noted at 02:29:13 that he arrived late to the meeting, exact arrival time unrecorded in digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the December 4, 2006 work session minutes with no corrections.

votes.item_title: Adopt Board of Health Resolution on Food and Lodging Inspection Fees (Item 7)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Commissioner Michael D. Page later noted at 02:29:13 that he arrived late to the meeting, exact arrival time unrecorded in digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted Board of Health resolution urging the General Assembly to grant counties authority to enact local food and lodging inspection fees to offset over $700,000 in annual inspection costs.

votes.item_title: Approve Existing Site Expansion and Roadway Improvements (Item 11)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; middle section of digest before 02:16:05 was truncated.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved small expansion of an existing approved site following public hearing remarks by Lee Lambert and commitments regarding stream buffers and roadway turn lanes.

votes.item_title: Approve Plan Amendment: Jovin, Northeast Creek (Item 12)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved technical Comprehensive Plan amendment correcting land use designation to match a prior June rezoning.

votes.item_title: Approve Plan Amendment: SECU East Durham (Item 13)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved technical Comprehensive Plan amendment for just over nine acres previously rezoned, prompted by a State Employees' Credit Union branch proposal.

votes.item_title: Adopt UDO Text Change: Repeal of Chain Link Fencing Standards (Item 14)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Repealed suburban and urban tier UDO chain-link fencing restrictions due to uneven contractor compliance and enforcement inequities.

votes.item_title: Approve Open Space and Trails Commission Matching Grants ($83,168) (Item 15)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved matching grant awards totaling $83,168 for four projects (Ellerbe Creek Watershed Association, Eno River Association, Watts Montessori PTA, and Eno Valley Elementary PTA).

votes.item_title: Excuse Commissioner Michael D. Page from January 22, 2007 Meeting
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Excused Commissioner Michael D. Page in advance from the January 22, 2007 meeting due to a conference conflict.

votes.item_title: Adjourn to Closed Session (NCDOT v. County of Durham)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; transcript ends at closed session motion.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding NCDOT v. County of Durham (04 CVS 6391).

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 11, 2006 Regular Session presided over by Chair Ellen W. Reckhow, the Durham Board of County Commissioners honored late civic leader Benjamin S. Ruffin, reaffirmed its 2003 Bill of Rights Defense Resolution, and unanimously (5-0) adopted both a legislative resolution supporting a phased increase in the compulsory school attendance age to 18 and its 2007 legislative package for the Durham delegation. On Item 10 (Boards and Commissions Appointments), the Board split 3-2 to remove and re-advertise Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority appointments amid debate over its three-consecutive-term limit policy (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Becky M. Heron, and Lewis A. Cheek; Nays: Michael D. Page and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr.). Earlier, the Board reviewed Consent Agenda Items 6A through 6H—including a $20 private-well lead sampling fee, $83,987 in Social Services grant funds, $1.38 million in public school capital building allocations, surplus property sales, and two donated conservation easements—before the surviving transcript truncated prior to a recorded consent vote. Following a unanimous closed session for an annual performance evaluation and economic development briefing, the Board returned to open session and voted 5-0 to set the County Manager's salary at $160,650 effective January 1, 2007.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Ellen W. Reckhow opened the December 11, 2006 Regular Session with the Pledge of Allegiance and noted a revised agenda, a revised legislative agenda with an added local item, and two additional resolutions. She announced Sheriff's Office recruitment for detention officers and deputy sheriffs, spring applications for Durham Neighborhood College due January 31, 2007, and Durham County Library's 2007 Durham Reads Together selection ('The Last Shot: City Streets, Basketball Dreams' by Darcy Frey), with library representative Susan Wright encouraging community participation.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (November 27, 2006 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow presented the minutes of the November 27, 2006 Regular Session and asked for any changes. On a motion by Vice Chair Becky M. Heron seconded by Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek, the Board approved the minutes unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 5A: Resolution in Recognition of Benjamin S. Ruffin
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Michael D. Page read a formal resolution honoring Durham native and civil rights leader Benjamin S. Ruffin, highlighting his leadership in 1960s civil rights protests, the Durham Housing Authority, the North Carolina Human Relations Council, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Company, Governor Jim Hunt's administration, and two terms as the first African American chairman of the UNC Board of Governors. Chair Reckhow shared personal recollections of serving alongside Ruffin on the Chamber of Commerce Human Relations Committee in the 1980s and stated the resolution and a personal letter would be sent to his family.

agenda_items.title: Item 5B: Bill of Rights Defense Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Reckhow read a resolution signed by all five commissioners reaffirming Durham County's September 22, 2003 Bill of Rights Defense Resolution and its commitment to protecting civil rights, free speech, privacy, due process, habeas corpus, and freedom from unreasonable searches and cruel and unusual punishment. A representative affiliated with the National Bill of Rights Defense Committee thanked the Board and shared contact information.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Consent Agenda Review (Items 6A through 6H)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed Consent Agenda items including a $20 public health user fee for private-well lead water sampling (6A), an $83,987 Social Services Home and Community Care Block Grant budget amendment (6B), business personal property listing deadline extensions (6C), and $1,380,000 in Public School Capital Building Fund allocations for Oak Grove Elementary, Southwest Elementary, Northern High, Brogden Middle, and Smith Elementary. Additional items covered upset-bid offers on county surplus properties (6E) and donated conservation easements from Wade and Carolyn Penny along the New Hope Creek corridor (6G) and Philip Blaylock in the Little River watershed (6H); the surviving transcript truncates before a formal consent vote is recorded.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Requesting Authority to Increase Compulsory School Attendance Age
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered a resolution urging the General Assembly to raise the compulsory school attendance age to 17 in school year 2008-2009 and to 18 or graduation in 2010-2011, implementing an action step from the dropout prevention plan discussed with the school superintendent. Speakers noted North Carolina's 60% graduation rate trailed the 70% national average and Durham's estimated rate stood near 57%; on a motion by Commissioner Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. seconded by Vice Chair Heron, the resolution passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Prisoner Reentry, Workforce Training, and 2007 Legislative Package
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed prisoner reentry needs, educational and vocational gaps among returning residents, Social Services funding for a Chamber of Commerce reentry coordinator, and hospitality workforce training tied to prepared food tax revenues ahead of a January 17 meeting with the Durham legislative delegation. On a motion by Commissioner Cheek seconded by Commissioner Page, the Board unanimously approved the 2007 legislative package including an added local support item relating to court fees.

agenda_items.title: Item 10: Appointments to Boards and Commissions and RDU Airport Authority Term-Limit Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Cheek moved, seconded by Vice Chair Heron, to remove and re-advertise the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority appointments because the Board's adopted policy bars citizens from serving more than three consecutive terms without a waiver and incumbent Steve Toler appeared to be in his fourth two-year term. Following discussion over clerk appointment records and past waivers, the motion passed 3-2 with Commissioners Page and Cousin dissenting, while Chair Reckhow also read out appointments for the Criminal Justice Partnership Act Advisory Committee, Environmental Affairs Board, Open Space and Trails Commission, and Public Health Board.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session for Public Officer Performance Review and Economic Development
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Commissioner Cheek seconded by Commissioner Page, the Board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to evaluate a public officer or employee and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss business or industry location or expansion.

agenda_items.title: County Manager Performance Review Report and 2007 Salary Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session, Chair Reckhow reported that the Board reviewed the County Manager's performance, commended his exemplary service over the past year, and reached consensus to set his salary at $160,650 effective January 1, 2007. On a motion by Commissioner Page seconded by Commissioner Cousin, the Board approved the salary unanimously before adjourning at 10:03 p.m.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously'). All five seated commissioners are confirmed present in the session.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes of the November 27, 2006 Regular Session with no changes.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted a resolution seeking General Assembly authority to raise the compulsory school attendance age to 17 in 2008-2009 and 18 or graduation in 2010-2011 as part of the dropout prevention plan.

votes.item_title: 2007 Legislative Package (Including Local Court Fees Support Item)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the County's 2007 legislative package for presentation to the Durham legislative delegation on January 17, incorporating an added local support item relating to court fees.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('motion carries unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved setting the County Manager's salary at $160,650 effective January 1, 2007 following his annual performance evaluation in closed session.

disagreements.meeting_title: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
disagreements.issue: Removal and Re-Advertisement of Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority Appointments Under Term-Limit Policy (Item 10)
disagreements.summary: The Board split 3-2 on Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek's motion, seconded by Vice Chair Becky M. Heron, to remove and re-advertise the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority appointments because incumbent Steve Toler appeared to have served beyond the Board's three-consecutive-term limit policy, while Commissioners Michael D. Page and Rev. Philip R. Cousin Jr. dissented.
disagreements.side_a_position: Remove the RDU Airport Authority appointment item and re-advertise the positions so the Board can follow its adopted term-limit policy and review all applicants before deciding whether to grant a waiver or revise the rule.
side_a_arguments: The Board previously adopted a policy resolution stating no citizen may serve more than three consecutive terms unless waived by the County Commissioners.
Appointment records differed on whether incumbent Steve Toler was appointed in 1999 or 2001, and Toler indicated he believed he was in his fourth two-year term.
Re-advertising lets the Board see what additional applicants come forward and examine whether the term-limit rule should be enforced or amended.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed removing and re-advertising the RDU Airport Authority appointments instead of proceeding with the scheduled appointments.
side_b_arguments: Voted against the motion to remove and re-advertise (specific floor remarks by the dissenting commissioners were omitted in gaps of the transcript digest, though Board discussion noted that both incumbent appointees had served with distinction and maintained strong communication, and that a prior waiver had been granted when Toler was in line to chair the Authority).
disagreements.resolution: Motion to remove and re-advertise the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority appointments passed 3-2; Chair Reckhow clarified that already-applied incumbents would remain on the ballot when it returned.
